Automaton_LargeWoodcutter_Desc: A rainpunk automaton that chops trees more efficiently, rarely needing to return to camp.
Biome_Bay_Description: These lands have been underwater for centuries, allowing a dense forest of algae to flourish. The surrounding seawater has almost completely cut off the area from the rest of the kingdom, leaving the nearby marshes almost untouched and full of the remains of ancient settlements.
Biome_Cave_Description: Giant underground caverns siphon rainwater from this strange depression, uncovering lands rich in minerals and ore, yet barren of life. It’s a sought-after destination for both traders and smugglers.
Biome_CoralForest_Description: The true source of the coral’s growth is unknown. Contrary to common belief, it doesn't usually appear in flooded regions. The unique influence of the coral mutates trees into distinctive strands that offer various resources.
Biome_CursedRoyalWoodlands_Description: A cursed area of the Royal Woodlands that is haunted by the lost souls of warriors fallen in the Great Civil War. The storm here is especially dangerous, and the forest more hostile than anywhere else. The Queen will handsomely reward any viceroy brave enough to settle this part of the world.
Biome_Moorlands_Description: A beautiful yet dangerous land that is colored a strange shade of crimson. It's called the Herb Garden of the Kingdom due to its abundance of herbs, berries, and roots.
Biome_Mushroom_Description: A harsh and cold land that has been claimed by many different, and extremely resilient species of fungi. The ground here is extremely hard and rocky, making it difficult to farm. This region is most famous for the giant organisms that can be found in its forests.
Biome_PoroBiome_Description: A lush, verdant expanse covered by an endless sea of bamboo trees. It is home to the magnificent Fluffbeaks - a species of gentle giants who love nothing more than to munch on the sweet stems and leaves of Tearsap Bamboo.
Biome_RoyalWoodlands_Description: The Queen's forests were once part of the Smoldering City, but the Blightstorm reclaimed this land. The Royal Woodlands are rich in roots, moss broccoli, mushrooms, and flax, with a decent amount of dewberries and clay. The ground is fertile and soft, which makes it perfect for farming.
Biome_SealedBiome_Description: Somewhere in this thick and dark forest, an ancient seal is hidden. Even the Ancients, in all their might and glory, couldn't defeat the creatures slumbering below - so they just imprisoned them. Over millennia, their sinister power gradually seeped to the surface, infecting the fauna and flora of this region. Viceroys don't embark here to establish settlements or gain reputation - their main goal is simply to find and close the seal.
Biome_Town_Moorlands_Description: A town specialized in herbalism. Provides access to grain, herb, stone and oil trade routes.
Biome_Town_Mushroom_Desc: A town surrounded by giant fungi. It provides access to grasscap mushroom, stone, clay, and meat trade routes.
Biome_Town_RoyalWoodlands_Desc: A town specialized in woodwork. It provides access to wood, plank, root, grasscap mushroom, and grain trade routes.
Biome_Wasteland_Description: Once a thriving forest of giant ashen trees, this land has been ravaged by relentless industrial exploitation and heavy mining, all driven by the lure of Thunderblight Shards - magically charged amber crystals used to craft cornerstones.
BiomeEffect_CursedGhosts_Desc: This land has seen a lot of bloodshed during the Great Civil War. Restless Spirits can be found in the forest.
BiomeEffect_CursedGlades_Desc: The forest has reshaped itself. It is impossible to recognize the danger of the glades, which are now all of even size.
BlightEffect_Faster_Move_Desc: Blightrot Cysts produce strange pollen that affects the craftsmen in this building. Workers move {0} faster.
BlightEffect_Production_Boost_Desc: The presence of Blightrot Cysts creates a strange aura within the building. Workers have a {0} chance of doubling their production.
BlightEffects_Unremovable_Desc: Blightrot grows on the structure, meaning there’s no safe way to destroy the building.
Bonuses_Desc: Increases the number of secondary resources collected from gathering nodes by {0}.
Branch_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_2A: I did it! I reforged the seal!
Branch_Core_AfterGoldSeal_5A: Maybe I'll finally take a break.
Branch_Core_AfterP10Seal_4: Aunt Lori, I wanted to ask you something. Has anyone ever <style=E1>seen</style> her?
Branch_Core_AfterP15Seal_4A: How does one join the Queen's Hand, exactly?
Branch_Core_AfterSilverSeal_3A: I think I'm finally getting the hang of this.
Branch_Core_AfterSilverSeal_8B: Are the seals made of different metals?
Branch_Core_FirstGameWon_5A: Yes, it does feel kinda weird...
Branch_Core_FirstGameWon_5B: Not necessarily. I like the change of scenery.
Branch_Core_InitialLate_4A: All this time... where were you?
Branch_Core_InitialMiddle_2A: Aunt Lori! What took you so long?
Branch_Core_InitialMiddle_6A: Isn't this supposed to be harder?
Branch_Core_IronmanPreSeal_4A: No, I don't think you have.
Branch_Core_IronmanStart_7A: I want to become a Queen's Hand.
Branch_Lore_Bats_2A: They don't beat around the bush. I like that.
Branch_Lore_Bats_2C: They seem a bit... crude. Difficult to deal with, even.
Branch_Lore_CoastalGrove_5A: How does this even work? How can a land just "appear"?
Branch_Lore_Criminals_11B: Whatever it takes to keep the Citadel safe.
Branch_Lore_Criminals_11C: I... I don't know. I hope I'll never be in that position.
Branch_Lore_Frogs_6B: If only they weren't so stubborn...
Branch_Lore_QueesHand_2B: It's the highest rank in the order, right?
Branch_Lore_Rain_2A: I don't know. It just... is?
Branch_Lore_SealedOnes1_2B: I heard people talking in the Svar Tavern about how they’re what's left of the Ancients.
Branch_Lore_SealedOnes1_2C: Not long ago, I met some cultists claiming that these Sealed Ones are... our gods.
Branch_Lore_SealedOnes2_2A: Yes, I remember you told me they've always been here.
Branch_Lore_SealedOnes2_2B: Yes, you said they may be what's left of the Ancients.
Branch_Lore_War1_3A: I don't think we would survive without her.
Branch_Lore_Zhorg_2B: Yes, I think I met Zhera, the treasurer.
Branch_Main_Lore: Can you tell me a story?
Branch_Main_Tips: I'm struggling a bit. Could you give me some advice?
Branch_Tip_Fishing_2A: I'm not really sure how to make use of them.
Branch_Tip_Services_2A: I didn't have the right blueprints.
Branch_Tip_Services_2C: There wasn't enough time to build any.
Branch_Tips_LostSettlerGames_2A: This whole Viceroy business... it's harder than I thought.
Branch_Tips_MoveCamps_2A: I didn't know I could do that.
Branch_Tips_RareTrading_2A: I don't like them. Their prices are too high.
Branch_Tips_WinningStreakOnLowDifficulty: It's alright. I'm enjoying myself, no need to worry.
Yes, it starts to feel repetitive.
Branch_Wiki_Adapt: I always seem to get the most useless blueprints...
Branch_Wiki_Blightrot: Tell me more about the Blightrot.
Branch_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock: How do I use Rain Engines?
Branch_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock: I heard some folks talking about Rainpunk. What is it?
Branch_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_No: No, I always thought it was useless.
Branch_Wiki_Resolve: Why are my villagers always unhappy?
Branch_Wiki_Trade: Can you explain how trading works?
Building_Altar_Description: An ancient altar to the Forsaken Gods. In the midst of the raging storm, you can make sacrifices here to gain unimaginable powers.
Building_BatHouse_Desc: A building specially designed for Bats. Must be built near a hearth. Fulfills the need for Bat Housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_BatsShrine_Desc: A court where villagers gather to choose the least welcome member of a given species and send them back to the Smoldering City - an act that increases the diligence of those who remain.
Building_BeaverHouse_Description: A building specially designed for Beavers. Must be built near a Hearth. Fulfills the need for Beaver housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_BigHaulersBase_Desc: A large hauler station employing 3 workers. Haulers move both production yields and crafting ingredients between buildings within the station's range.
Building_BiomeBlackMarket_Desc: With resources stretched so thin in the kingdom, the penalty for contraband is death. Yet, where there’s a need, there’s a way - the Black Amber Syndicate thrives by catering to those settling in the harshest of regions.
Building_BiomeGrassSpawner_Description: An artificial patch of fertile land with a pre-built farm field on top. Leaves behind Fertile Soil when destroyed.
Building_BiomePerkCrafter_Desc: An ancient forge used by the Crown for generations to craft cornerstones from Thunderblight Shards. Now it stands abandoned, its fires long cold, but its legacy still felt in the region.
Building_BiomePoro_Desc: Fluffbeaks are gentle creatures that rarely attack unless provoked. They cannot be domesticated and freely choose which caravan to "join". Many settlements in this region have failed simply because no Fluffbeak was willing to settle nearby.
Building_BlightBomb_Desc: A strange device known as a Blight Bomb. Best not to place it too close to the Ancient Hearth...
Building_BlightPost_Desc: A specialized building dedicated to fighting Blightrot. Blight Fighters will prepare <sprite name="blight fuel"> Purging Fire during drizzle and clearance seasons, and use it to burn Blightrot Cysts during the storm.
Building_Camp_Generic_Description: An advanced gathering camp. Can collect resources from large and giant gathering nodes in addition to small ones. Can collect: {0}.
Building_ClayPit_Description:
Uses Clearance Water to produce goods regardless of the season. Must be placed on fertile soil. Can produce: {0}
Rain engine: {1}.
Building_CloakedWandererShrine_BuildingD: A strange, ancient altar, supposedly dedicated to the Holy Flame. Grants access to temporary support abilities.
Building_CloakedWandererShrine_EffectDes: An enigmatic obsidian tablet etched with intricate blueprints. Unlocks the Flame Altar - an ancient building that grants access to temporary support abilities.
Building_CopperRoad_Description: A road reinforced with copper. Grants a 25% speed increase to villagers. Road construction cost is not affected by effects, modifiers, or perks.
Building_Decoration_Aesthetics_Desc: <color=#8AAFFD>Aesthetics.</color> The more a settlement grows, the more demand there is for beauty. Decorations are used to level up Hearths.
Building_Decoration_Comfort_Desc: <color=#49E058>Comfort.</color> Even the most rudimentary encampment needs distractions. Decorations are used to level up Hearths.
Building_Decoration_GroundwaterExtractor: <color=#8AAFFD>Aesthetics.</color> A curious piece of improvised technology. It extracts moisture from the soil around it and converts it into 10 <sprite name="[water] clearance water"> Clearance Water per minute.
Building_Decoration_Harmony_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> Peace of mind can be as important as shelter and food in these harsh lands. Decorations are used to level up Hearths.
Building_Decorations_ScoreCount: Counts as {0} decorations of its type.
Building_Farmfield_Description: Can only be placed on fertile soil. Requires a Small Farm, Plantation, Herb Garden, Forester's Hut, Brineworks, or Homestead nearby to produce crops.
Building_FishingHut_Desc: An advanced fishing hut. Can fish in large fishing ponds in addition to small ones. Can catch: {0}.
Building_FlawlessWorkshop_Desc:
An upgraded production building with all recipes at the highest grade. Can produce: {0}.
Rain engine: {1}.
Building_ForagersCamp_Description: Starting point for foragers going out into the wild to gather {0}.
Building_FoxHouse_Description: A building specially designed for Foxes. Must be built near a Hearth. Fulfills the need for Fox housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_FrogHouse_Description: A building specially designed for Frogs. Must be built near a Hearth. Fulfills the need for Frog housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_GenericFarm_Boosted_Description: Uses nearby farm fields to grow {0}. Has improved efficiency and more worker slots.
Building_GenericFarm_Description: Uses nearby farm fields to grow {0}.
Building_GenericInstitution_Desc: A place where villagers can fulfill their need for:{0}.
Building_Greenhouse_Description: Uses Drizzle Water to grow crops regardless of the season. Must be placed on fertile soil. Can produce: {0}
Building_Grove_Description: Uses nearby farm fields to produce {0}.
Building_Guidestone_Desc: It is not known where the guidance stones came from or what their original purpose was, but they are imbued with magic and always point in the direction of a nearby seal.
Building_HallowedFarm_Description: Uses nearby farm fields to produce {0}. Has improved production and more worker slots.
Building_HarpyHouse_Desc: A building specially designed for Harpies. Must be built near a Hearth. Fulfills the need for Harpy housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_HarvesterCamp_Desc: Starting point for harvesters going out into the wild to gather {0}.
Building_Hearth_Description: The heart of the colony is protected by the Holy Flame. Villagers gather here to rest, eat, and receive clothing. If the fire goes out, people will lose hope.
Building_HearthBuildable_Description: Reduces Hostility and serves as a meeting place. Villagers gather here to rest, eat, and receive clothing. If the fire goes out, people will use another Hearth instead. Can't be built too close to other Hearths.
Building_HerbalistCamp_Description: Starting point for herbalists going out into the wild to gather {0}.
Building_HerbGarden_Description: Uses nearby farm fields to produce {0}.
Building_HolyInstitution_Desc: An upgraded service building with an additional passive effect. Villagers can use it to fulfill their need for: {0}.
Building_Homestead_Description: Uses a large area of nearby farm fields to grow {0}.
Building_HumanHouse_Description: A building specially designed for Humans. Must be built near a Hearth. Fulfills the need for Human housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_Hydrant_Desc: A small storage for <sprite name="blight fuel"> Purging Fire. Blight Fighters will use it to restock their fuel when fighting Blightrot in the storm.
Building_InstituteOfArcheology_Desc: A building designed to help you study the past. Can be upgraded to locate archaeological discoveries or improve the settlement's exploration capabilities.
Building_LizardHouse_Description: A building specially designed for Lizards. Must be built near a Hearth. Fulfills the need for Lizard housing and can accommodate {0} inhabitants.
Building_LoreTablet1_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> Born in the Blightstorm, she will climb the Red Mountain. The fires beneath her feet shall hiss her name.
Building_LoreTablet2_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> Though sealed beneath the muddy ground, their voices ring loud and clear. Maddening, alluring.
Building_LoreTablet3_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> The true rulers of this world shall rise again and break the seals that bind them.
Building_LoreTablet4_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> Envy the lesser species, for they do not yet know what lies beneath. But in time, they will understand.
Building_LoreTablet5_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> It pours, yet it does not flood. As if the earth itself greedily drinks every last drop of this eternal curse.
Building_LoreTablet6_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> Embrace the Eternal Rain, for it powers the engine of progress.
Building_LoreTablet7_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> Don't let the pleasant sparking of the raindrops fool you. This is just the first sign of your flesh rotting.
Building_MainStorage_Description: Stores a large amount of goods and protects them from the rain. Workers always deliver and take goods from the Warehouse nearest to them.
Building_Mine_Description: Can only be placed on coal, copper, or salt veins. Can produce: {0}.
Building_Monolith_Desc: <color=#8AAFFD>Aesthetics.</color> The symbols carved into this monumental stone bear an eerie resemblance to the forest and corruption. Decreases Hostility by 10 points and increases the Ancient Hearth's resistance by 100.
Building_NoriaRainpunk_Desc: <color=#49E058>Comfort.</color> The old machine has been improved with Rainpunk technology. Farm production becomes easier.
Building_Path_Description: A simple path, doesn't cost any resources. Grants a 5% speed increase to villagers.
Building_Plantation_Description: Uses nearby farm fields to produce {0}.
Building_Port_Desc: From this port, expeditions can be launched to search the nearby swamps for blueprints and treasure in the submerged ruins of former settlements.
Building_PrimitiveCamp_Desc: A small, crude version of a specialized gathering camp. It's slower, and can only collect resources from small gathering nodes. Can collect: {0}.
Building_PrimitiveFishingHut_Desc: A crude version of a normal fishing hut. It's slower, and can only fish in small fishing ponds. Can catch: {0}.
Building_RainCollector_Description: Collects rainwater used for crafting and powering Rain Engines in production buildings. The type of rainwater collected changes with the season. Has a tank capacity of 50.
Building_RainCollectorBig_Desc: Collects rainwater used for crafting and powering Rain Engines in production buildings. The type of rainwater collected changes with the season. Produces twice as much as a regular collector and has double the tank capacity (100).
Building_RainpunkFactory_Description:
A very advanced piece of technology. Can produce {0}.
Rain engine: {1}.
Building_RuinsOfNoria_Desc: An old but surprisingly advanced construction. Bitten by the tooth of time and destroyed by raging storms.
Building_ScavengerCamp_Description: Starting point for scavengers going out into wild to gather {0}.
Building_Seal_Desc: Evil has survived. The Sealed Ones enter our realm through this broken seal. Terrible plagues are sent to destroy us. Collect the lost fragments of the Ancient Guardian to summon it and close the seal.
Building_SealedBiomeShrine_Desc: A powerful, ancient structure that allows you to summon aid directly from the Citadel. Grants access to three types of temporary support abilities.
Building_Shelter_Description: Can accommodate most villagers, but won't satisfy the need for species-specific housing. Has to be built near a Hearth. Can house {0} residents.
Building_SmallFarm_Description: Uses a small number of farm fields nearby to produce {0}.
Building_SmallHaulersBase_Desc: A small hauler station employing 1 worker. Haulers move both production yields and crafting ingredients between buildings within the station's range.
Building_StonecuttersCamp_Description: Starting point for stonecutters going out into the wild to gather {0}.
Building_StoneRoad_Description: A road made out of stone. Grants a 15% speed increase to villagers. Road construction cost is not affected by effects, modifiers, or perks.
Building_TemporaryEngineeringStation_Des: A makeshift workstation designed by the Brass Order. It’s far simpler than their sophisticated machinery back in the Citadel, but it’ll get the job done.
Building_TermiteNest_Desc: <color=#D6E54A>Harmony.</color> A contained stonetooth termite burrow. Provides 5 <sprite name="[food raw] insects"> Insects per minute.
Building_TradingPost_Description: Traders from the Smoldering City can station here and offer their wares.
Building_TrappersCamp_Description: Starting point for trappers going out into the wild to collect {0}.
Building_WaterExtractor_Desc: Used to extract and pump infused rainwater through underground pipes to production buildings, where it can be used to increase productivity. Must be placed on an active geyser. Has a tank capacity of 50.
Building_WoodcuttersCamp_Description: Starting point for woodcutters going out into the wild to cut down trees.
BuildingPerk_Automaton_Description: A rainpunk automaton will permanently occupy one workplace. It doesn't eat, and it doesn't need rest. Its sole purpose is to work. Automatons have no chance of producing double yields.
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_Automaton_Desc: A rainpunk automaton will help Blight Fighters burn Blightrot Cysts during the storm. It doesn't eat and doesn't need to rest. Blight Automatons can't produce <sprite name="blight fuel"> Purging Fire.
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_BlightFighterSpe: A more compact version of the famous Blight Fighter flamethrower. Blight Fighters assigned to this Blight Post move {0} faster.
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_CystBurnSpeed_De: An innovative improvement to the flamethrower ignition system. Blight Fighters and Blight Automatons at this Blight Post need {0} seconds less to burn a Blightrot Cyst.
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_CystGenerationRa: Blight Fighters regularly inspect production buildings. For each Blight Fighter assigned to a building with this upgrade, Blightrot Cysts will appear {0} slower when using Rain Engines (up to a maximum of 90%).
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_PurgingFireProdS: Only the most experienced Blight Fighters can operate this machine. Workers at this Blight Post have a {0} higher chance of producing twice the amount of <sprite name="blight fuel"> Purging Fire.
BuildingPerk_ExtractorTank_Description: Increases tank capacity for the corresponding rainwater type by {0}.
BuildingPerk_HighlightArcheology1_Descri: Reveals the location of the closest archaeological discovery.
BuildingPerk_HighlightArcheology2_Descri: Reveals the location of the second closest archaeological discovery.
BuildingPerk_HighlightArcheology3_Descri: Reveals the location of the farthest archaeological discovery.
BuildingPerk_RainpunkComfortable_Desc: Work is much easier with Rain Engines on. Workers gain +5 to Resolve.
BuildingPerk_RainpunkExtraChance_Desc: Increases the chance for extra production yields by {0}.
BuildingPerk_ReplaceRainpunkEffects_Desc: Rain Engine production bonuses are twice as strong ({0} production speed, {1} double yield chance).
BuildingPerk_Woodcutter_Capacity_Desc: A special wooden frame that makes transporting resources a lot easier. Woodcutters working in a camp with this upgrade can carry {0} more items of the same type.
BuildingPerk_Woodcutter_ExtraProd_Desc: No tree or stump goes to waste. Woodcutters in this camp have a {0} higher chance of producing double yields.
BuildingPerk_Woodcutter_Speed_Desc: Specially reinforced boots that are surprisingly lightweight. Woodcutters working in a camp with this upgrade move {0} faster.
BuildingPerk_Woodcutter_StorageAutomaton: An automated hauling cart will help woodcutters transport resources from the Woodcutters' Camp to the Warehouse.
Cart_BlightFighterCartDesc: A rainpunk automaton helping Blight Fighters burn Blightrot Cysts.
Cart_Hauler_Desc: An automated hauling cart helping transport resources between buildings.
Cart_LumberCart_Desc: An automated hauling cart that helps woodcutters transport resources.
Cart_Minecart_Desc: An automated minecart helping miners transport resources.
Citadel_Structure_Monastery_Name_Ironman: Monastery of the Vigilant Flame Expansion
Common_DLCLocked_Bats_Desc: You need to own the "Nightwatchers" DLC to unlock this.
Common_DLCLocked_Frogs_Desc: You need to own the "Keepers of the Stone" DLC to unlock this.
Common_Ironman_Locked: Locked in the Queen's Hand Trial.
ConditionalNeedEffect_1BuildingDestroyed: The storm in this region is extremely violent. Once this effect is activated, you'll have to pay {1} {0} (multiplied by the number of years). If you don't, 3 buildings in your settlement will become ruins.
ConditionalNeedEffect_3BuildingsDestroye: A terrifying sound from a raging sky. Every {0} seconds, {1} buildings are destroyed by lightning.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Aurora_Desc: The weather in these lands sometimes enables you to peer beyond the veil of clouds.
ConditionalNeedEffect_BitterRain_Desc: A cold, half-frozen sleet is falling from the sky.
ConditionalNeedEffect_BlightrotAfterDeat: This damp and rotting landscape is the perfect breeding ground for sickness. Every villager that dies during the storm instantly turns into a Blood Flower.
ConditionalNeedEffect_BuildingMaterialsP: The rain dissolves some of the resources transported to your Warehouse. Recipes producing building materials yield {0} fewer goods.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Cloudburst_Desc: Even the hardiest villagers need some sort of cover in this weather.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ColdFront_Desc: The wind is bone-chillingly cold, making every exposed bit of skin sting painfully after just a few moments.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ColdSnap_Desc: A sudden drop of temperature can cause extreme hunger.
ConditionalNeedEffect_DeadlyLights_Desc: Those lured by the lights may not come back. It's better to keep people focused and occupied.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Downpour_Desc: The heavy rain and cold climate are extremely taxing on the villagers. Without proper shelter and nourishment, the people will have to compensate somehow.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Eclipse_Desc: The sun is obscured even more than usual. Almost as if it's gone missing for a while.
ConditionalNeedEffect_EerieSong_Desc: There are no words, or even a melody. Those who go looking for the song don't usually return...
ConditionalNeedEffect_EuphoricVapours_De: There is something in the air that invokes pleasant moods. The effect is especially strong when the body is well nourished.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Fog_Desc: A veil of moisture obscures vision. It is hard to walk in these conditions.
ConditionalNeedEffect_FoorProdSpeedSlowe: The rain smells like Blightrot... Global food production is slowed by {0} per Hostility level (counting from level 0).
ConditionalNeedEffect_FreshBreeze_Desc: A refreshing gust of air lifts the spirit. Those with their basic needs taken care of are more willing to work.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Generic_Status: To PREVENT it, fulfill the following need(s): {0}
ConditionalNeedEffect_Generic_Status_Pos: To GAIN it, fulfill the following need(s): {0}
ConditionalNeedEffect_GoodsForTrade_Desc: The Queen's generosity knows no limits. Gain {1} every time you sell goods worth {0} Amber.
ConditionalNeedEffect_GrowingFoodConsump: Working in this environment requires a lot of energy. Villagers have a higher chance of consuming twice the amount of food on each break ({0} for each Hostility level, counting from level 0).
ConditionalNeedEffect_GrowingServiceCons: Some goods seem to be mysteriously disappearing. Maybe there's a thief in the settlement? Villagers have a higher chance of consuming twice the amount of goods when using services ({0} for each Hostility level, counting from level 0).
ConditionalNeedEffect_Hailstorm_Desc: Death by a thousand hailstones. There is no way to be safe without a roof over your head.
ConditionalNeedEffect_InkInCollector_Des: The rain in this region has a weird red hue and iron taste to it. <sprite name="[crafting] pigment"> Pigment ({0}) can be collected in the Rain Collector in drizzle season.
ConditionalNeedEffect_InsectsInScavenger: Insects are extremely easy to collect after heavy rainfall. During drizzle season, workers in the Scavengers' Camp can gather <sprite name="[food raw] insects"> insects ({0}) from insect nodes.
ConditionalNeedEffect_InvigoratingWinds_: The smell of fresh air. Energizing for those not distracted by its coldness.
ConditionalNeedEffect_LessMetalProduced_: Acid rain is slowly eating away at all metal objects. Producing Copper Bars, Crystalized Dew, and all goods that use metal ingots yields {0} fewer goods.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Melancholy_Desc: A humdrum and peaceful atmosphere brings back memories of the Citadel: home cooked meals and cozy beds.
ConditionalNeedEffect_MoreDepositCharges: Small, energizing drops cause uncontrollable growth in certain species. All gathering nodes discovered during drizzle season have more charges: +{0} to small ones, and +{1} to large ones.
ConditionalNeedEffect_NauseousSpores_Des: A sickening smell is in the air. Villagers need something to help them focus.
ConditionalNeedEffect_NoImpatienceReduct: Harsh weather conditions make it impossible to reach the Citadel. Gaining Reputation doesn't lower Impatience.
ConditionalNeedEffect_PiercingWinds_Desc: Extremely strong winds make it difficult to sustain the Holy Flame. Fuel consumption in Hearths is increased by {0}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_RegularStorm_Desc: Homeless villagers are especially vulnerable during the storm.
ConditionalNeedEffect_RepFromResolveBloc: No amount of amenities can distract villagers from the terrifying storm. Reputation generated from Resolve grows {0} slower.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ResinForWood_Desc: A red, sticky substance is oozing out from beneath the tree bark. Gain {0} every time woodcutters cut down a tree.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SlowGathering_Desc: The ground is moving and swaying from all the rainwater it’s absorbed. Gathering speed is decreased by {0}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SlowWoodCutting_De: The trees seem to come to life during the storm... Woodcutting is {0} slower, but each fallen tree gives {1}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SpeedGathering_Des: The forest's fruits are so ripe, they almost fall into the basket on their own. Gathering speed is increased by {0}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_StrangeLights_Desc: People are reporting seeing strange visages in the woods. They need something to put their minds at ease.
ConditionalNeedEffect_StrangeVisions_Des: They offer inspiration for open minds...
ConditionalNeedEffect_SunFestivities_Des: Having ways to celebrate and express themselves keeps people more eager to work for the common good.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SwarmsBad_Desc: Constant bites and cuts don't really hurt that much, but are certainly annoying for those without proper protection.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ToxicRain_Desc: Everything grows and blooms under this heavy rainfall, even if it shouldn't.
ConditionalNeedEffect_UnderTheOpenSky_De: Lack of shelter during such a malevolent storm is simply gross neglect of villagers.
ConditionalNeedEffect_WoodcutterCapacity: The evaporating rainwater has made the wood a lot lighter in this region. Woodcutters can carry {1} more goods in drizzle season.
ConditionalNeedEffect_WoodPaymentForVill: Only the Sacred Flame can protect the settlement from the darkness surrounding it. Pay {1} {0} for every villager in your settlement. If you don't pay for all of them, 2 people will leave.
If you don't deliver the required goods for the sacrifice, {0} villagers will disappear.
Content_Tip_CameraRotation: Use the middle mouse button to rotate the camera.
Content_Tip_Cycle: The Cycle is a vicious force of nature that ravages the land every few years. The time left before the next Blightstorm is indicated on the bottom of the screen in the World Map view.
Content_Tip_DangerousGlades: Dangerous glades are always marked. They are rich in resources and rewards, but be sure you're prepared to deal with the threats they contain.
Content_Tip_Destruction: Destroying a building will refund all the resources that were spent on its construction.
Content_Tip_MovingBuildings: You can move some buildings by selecting the 'Move' button in the building window.
Content_Tip_Expansion: You can build Small Hearths and Warehouses to expand your settlement - villagers will always rest at the nearest Hearth, and take their goods to the nearest Warehouse.
Content_Tip_Factions: Different factions are constantly trying to settle on the World Map. If they succeed, they will drain Citadel Resources from nearby areas.
Content_Tip_Fuel: Wood isn't the only thing that can be burned in the hearth. There are also other, more efficient types of fuel like oil and coal.
Content_Tip_Lore1: The never-ending rain carries a magical charge with it. It's dangerous, but very useful at the same time, and can be used to create powerful Rainpunk technology.
Content_Tip_Lore2: The Smoldering City is the only safe haven in the known world. It was built on ancient ruins, left behind by the long-dead Great Civilization.
Content_Tip_Lore3: The Marshlands are considered by scholars to be one giant underground fungus. Some even claim that it is sentient.
Content_Tip_Lore4: Clearance is the warmest season. The rain is light, and there's even a bit of sunshine during the day. It's the ideal time for harvesting crops.
Content_Tip_Lore5: The storm is a time of destruction and chaos. Strong winds and relentless rainfall make it difficult to work outside.
Content_Tip_Lore6: Drizzle is the calmest season - a time of growth and regeneration. The rain is heavy, but its negative effects are milder than during the rest of the year.
Content_Tip_Modifiers: Some areas of the world have special modifiers. These objects make it harder to win, but also give better rewards.
Content_Tip_Moodlets: Every map has its own Forest Mysteries - special seasonal effects that will influence your settlements. Beneficial Forest Mysteries trigger during drizzle season, while dangerous ones are active during the storm.
Content_Tip_NeedCycle: Are your villagers hungry even though you have food in your Warehouse? Just wait for them to rest at the Hearth. Then they’ll have chance to satisfy their needs.
Content_Tip_NewContent: You unlock new buildings, cornerstones, and traders by leveling up. The higher the difficulty of a game, the more experience points you’ll earn.
Content_Tip_Recipes: Most recipes have variable ingredients. This allows you to switch between different input goods, yet achieve the same result.
Content_Tip_ReputationPoints: Reputation Points can be acquired by completing orders, finishing Glade Events, and keeping your villagers' Resolve very high.
Content_Tip_Resting: Villagers need breaks. They will regularly return to the Hearth to rest and fulfill their needs.
Content_Tip_Storage: Each resource in a building has its own storage limit. When a resource reaches its limit, it will be moved to a warehouse.
Content_Tip_TraderAssault: Don't have enough Amber for a trade? You can always assault a trader and rob them. But beware, this has dire consequences!
Content_Tip_Upgrades: You can spend the Citadel Resources you’ve acquired to buy upgrades in the Smoldering City.
Content_Tutorial3_LockedReason: To unlock the Rainpunk & Blightrot tutorial scenario, you must first buy the Obsidian Archive Level 6 upgrade in the Smoldering City.

CycleEffect_RainpunkShredder_Desc: When activated, adds a Rainpunk Shredder to every Woodcutters' Camp in the settlement. This large automaton can fell multiple trees without returning to camp. Can be triggered from the Main Warehouse.

CycleEffect_WeCornerstonesRerrolls_Desc: Viceroys face punishment all the time, but the Order prefers to handle it themselves rather than trust the judgment of the common folk. Their gratitude, however - like the medal they gave you - is fleeting. Grants an extra cornerstone reroll.
