Dialogue_CommonOpening2: Let me just sit here for a short while.
Dialogue_CommonOpening4: Look who it is. <style=N1>Lori smiles softly.</style>
Dialogue_CommonReturn1: Anything else you want to talk about?
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_1: Well, aren't you in a good mood? <style=N1>Lori looks at you with interest.</style> Any news to share?
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_3: Will you look at that... <style=N1>Her face lights up in a sincere smile.</style> You actually made it!
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_4: Well done. That must have been quite the challenge.
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_5: But as much as I hate to burst your bubble... you should know that it is not the end of your journey. This is only the beginning.
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_7A: So far, you've only reforged the Bronze Seal. And while this is undoubtedly an admirable feat, there are still other, more menacing seals out there.
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_8: <style=N1>Lori's eyes sparkle with pride.</style> Keep it up, kid. You're a fast learner.
Dialogue_Core_AfterBronzeSeal_9: The Crown has already recognized your efforts. A little more, and you may even be allowed to venture near the Gold Seal one day.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_1: You did it! You actually did it! <style=N1>Aunt Lori shakes her head in feigned disbelief.</style> I'm impressed.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_10: Just... please be careful. Don't rush headfirst into an Adamantine Seal.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_2: You've managed to reforge the Gold Seal... so you know what that means, right? This is your key to the higher ranks of the Order!
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_3: Not to mention how much you've contributed to the kingdom. The people of the Citadel owe you much.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_4: So, after such a remarkable achievement... have you thought about what you want to do next?
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_6A: <style=N1>A hearty laugh escapes Lori's lips as she nods in agreement.</style> Definitely. You've earned it.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_6B: I see you haven't lost your enthusiasm. Good. <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out a sincere laugh.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_6C: You don't have to make a decision right away. Take your time.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_7A: Most Viceroys don't even make it this far, so take as much time as you need. And if retirement ever feels too mundane, there’ll be new challenges waiting for you.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_7B: If you're still eager to continue assisting your brothers and sisters on the front lines, I have an intriguing proposition for you.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_7C: Rest, enjoy the moment... and when you're ready, you can decide whether to take on new challenges.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_8: With your newly earned rank, you’ve gained the right to work with so-called Seal Contracts.
Dialogue_Core_AfterGoldSeal_9: Special agreements between you and the Crown. They allow you to choose which seals you want to tackle each cycle.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_1: Don't say anything. I've already heard the news...
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_10: Or, maybe you'll just finally be able to take a break... <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out a hearty laugh.</style> I know many Viceroys whose only dream is to retire.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_11: Think about it. <style=N1>Aunt Lori's lips curve into a kind, encouraging smile.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_2: <style=N1>Aunt Lori stands tall, a look of pride on her face.</style> You actually did it, you blighted devil! You reforged the Lead Seal!
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_3: I knew you were talented, but I didn't think you could handle another seal so quickly.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_4: Listen, you seem awfully determined. <style=N1>Aunt Lori squints her eyes, looking you up and down for a second.</style> I think I have something that might interest you.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_5: According to tradition, the Gold Seal has always been considered the final proving ground for new Viceroys.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_6: And for good reason. Only those who have mastered this profession to perfection are capable of reforging it.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_7: You still have a long way to go, but... why not try?
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_8: You’d certainly be doing the kingdom a great service. Each reforged seal weakens the Blightstorm... buys us a little more time.
Dialogue_Core_AfterLeadSeal_9: And if you succeed, you’ll be promoted to a higher rank within the Order. You may even be given the privilege of mentoring a student of your own.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_2: <style=N1>For a moment, Lori's eyes flash with pride.</style> Very few have made it this far, you know?
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_3: And I'm sure news of your accomplishments has already reached the queen's ears... may the Flame bless her soul.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_5: <style=N1>Lori's nose and eyebrows crinkle in a strange grimace.</style> What a ridiculous question.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_6: You seem to have let your recent successes go to your head. <style=N1>She shakes her head.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_7: Just... leave it, and don't concern yourself with this. You should know your place...
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_8: <style=N1>Tension leaves Lori's face as she composes herself.</style> I'm sorry...
Dialogue_Core_AfterP10Seal_9: I really am... I shouldn't be so hard on you. This is a day of celebration, after all.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_1: Ha! Another seal closed I see!
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_10: But this is not a topic for idle conversation. And it's not something that should concern you. Do you understand?
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_12: So it's settled. <style=N1>She gives you a warm, but forced smile.</style> You should get some rest now, you've earned it.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_13: Maybe visit the Svar? I'm sure everyone will want to buy you a round after today.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_2: And I've heard from the caravaneers unpacking at the Pioneer's Gate that you did a great job!
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_3: They all sang your praises. "A Hand couldn't have done any better", they said.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_5: <style=N1>Lori maintains a smile, but the warmth doesn't quite reach her eyes anymore.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_6: You don't just join the Queen's Hands. You become one.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_7: And you stay one for the rest of your life...
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_8: ...a rather short life in most cases. <style=N1>Her lips tighten, the smile now completely gone.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterP15Seal_9: Queen's Hands are thrust into the heart of the most brutal storms, their lives offered up for the cause.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP20Seal_1: <style=N1>Aunt Lori doesn't say anything. She just looks at you, her expression beaming with pride.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterP20Seal_2: Your name came up in today's briefing! <style=N1>Her voice is slightly distorted by the unusually wide smile on her face.</style> I'm so proud of you!
Dialogue_Core_AfterP20Seal_3: You've really done it! By closing the Adamantine Seal, you’ve reached the highest rank in the Order!
Dialogue_Core_AfterP20Seal_4: <style=N1>Her eyes glisten slightly from the tears she’s holding back.</style> If only your mother could see you now... She would be so proud. I know I am.
Dialogue_Core_AfterP20Seal_5: With a generation like yours, we may actually have a chance against the never-ending storm...
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_1: There you are. Just in time. <style=N1>Aunt Lori's face lights up with a welcoming smile.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_10: The Ancients were masters of metallurgy. They forged tools and constructed architectural marvels with such efficiency that it seemed they could manipulate the very states of matter at will.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_11: We can barely create crystalized dew consistently, while copper smelting continues to pose a substantial logistical challenge for us all.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_12: But the Ancients... They knew something we don't. A way to harness the extraordinary properties of rain to create the most durable alloys.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_13: Maybe someday we'll catch up to them... but for now, we have to deal with the threat they left us.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_14: <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out an amused sigh.</style> But enough of that. Let's focus on the issue at hand instead.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_15: It appears you're finally ready to take on the Gold Seal. It'll be a tough one - but I'm sure you can handle it.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_2: I heard you reforged another Seal. How was it?
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_4A: I can see that! You're outpacing all the other initiates.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_4B: <style=N1>Lori is silent for a moment, nodding.</style>
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_5B: And it's only going to get harder... But from what I see, you're doing well.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_6B: You can always invest a little more in the Citadel's ongoing construction projects. This will likely earn you some additional support from the Crown.
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_7: Let me ask you this - have you ever wondered why there are different types of seals? What their names mean?
Dialogue_Core_AfterSilverSeal_9B: Exactly! But it's not that simple.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameLost_1: I can see in your eyes that your last expedition didn't go too well... <style=N1>Aunt Lori gives you a subtle, concerned look.</style>
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameLost_2: Don't worry, that's just the way things are. You learn from your mistakes.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameLost_3: When I was just starting out, I brought my first three settlements to ruin before the third storm even arrived.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameLost_4: <style=N1>Lori smiles gently.</style> Don't beat yourself up over this. You’ll figure it out eventually.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameLost_5: Just try to remember your training. Food, fuel, careful exploration, trade, and hostility management.... The five basic factors.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameLost_6: Once you get more practice, I'm sure you’ll be reforging seals in no time.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_1: Well, if it isn't my favorite {P:nephew/niece}! <style=N1>Lori's eyes light up with excitement.</style>
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_3: Does it matter? <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out a hearty laugh.</style> We have reason to celebrate! I hear you did pretty well with your first settlements!
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_4: Feels weird, huh? Investing so much time and energy into a town, and then leaving it as soon as it becomes self-sufficient.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_6A: It does, doesn't it? But with the Blightstorm constantly on our heels, there’s never enough time to linger.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_6B: Oh... <style=N1>Aunt Lori raises an eyebrow.</style> Interesting. Usually, new Viceroys aren't so eager to move on.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_7A: After all, we aren't really governors or settlers. We are pioneers, meant only to take the first step and leave the boring bureaucracy to others.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_7B: But that's good! You seem to be getting used to this new life quite quickly.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_8A: <style=N1>Lori's lips curl into a warm smile.</style> I'm sure you'll get used to it.
Dialogue_Core_FirstGameWon_9: And who knows, maybe someday you’ll join our brothers and sisters on the frontier, in their never-ending fight against the Sealed Ones.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_1: <style=N1>As soon as you step into your new home, you notice a richly clothed woman standing by the window, her gaze fixed on the Citadel.</style>
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_10: Allow yourself to make mistakes. It'll get much easier as you go along.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_11: Oh, and sweetie... This house looks a bit... empty. See if you can find something to decorate the place with.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_2: Finally, kid! I was beginning to worry you’d been eaten by a storming mole.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_3: <style=N1>Lori looks around the empty room.</style> Well, isn't this a nice-looking house? Back in my day, fresh viceroys would sleep on the floor of the Svar Tavern.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_6A: Don't let your guard down, kiddo. The outer wilds are never a safe place. The farther you travel from the Citadel and her presence, the tougher it gets.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_6B: <style=N1>Lori smiles at you gently.</style> I remember I failed my first three assignments. Chin up! You're not alone in this.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_6C: I know, dear. There's a lot to take in at once — so many new things, and so little time. <style=N1>Lori exhales softly.</style> Learning can feel like climbing a mountain.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_7: I promised my sister I would look after you, and I plan on keeping that promise.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_8: As a member of the Queen's Hands, there is much I can teach you, but knowledge is of no value unless you put it into practice.
Dialogue_Core_InitialFresh_9: For now, focus on exploration. Try new things. Venture into uncharted territory.
Dialogue_Core_InitialLate_3: There you are! I was beginning to worry.
Dialogue_Core_InitialLate_5: I'm sorry, dear. It wasn't up to me. I wish I could've been here for you...
Dialogue_Core_InitialLate_6: To see all the wonderful things you've achieved, and be able to help you on your way.
Dialogue_Core_InitialLate_7: I promised my sister I'd look after you, but from what I've heard, you've been doing quite well on your own.
Dialogue_Core_InitialLate_8: But still - remember that I am always here for you. Don't be afraid to ask questions. <style=N1>A warm smile lights up Aunt Lori's face.</style> And again, it's so good to finally see you.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_3A: Here you are! I'm sorry, dear, there were... some things I needed to take care of first.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_4: <style=N1>Lori looks around the empty room.</style> Well, isn't this a nice-looking house? Back in my day, only the highest-ranking Viceroys had their own quarters.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_5: How are you doing so far?
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_7A: <style=N1>Lori bellows with laughter.</style> Well, I can see some insignia are still missing from your coat.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_7B: <style=N1>Lori's eyes flash with a glimpse of pride.</style> Then you already know what it means to be a true Viceroy.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_7C: There is no shame in that. Don't let those fools in the Svar tell you otherwise.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_8A: Don't let your guard down, kiddo. There are still plenty of things out there that can surprise even a Queen's Hand.
Dialogue_Core_InitialMiddle_8C: Don't hesitate to ask me if you have any questions.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_10: Maybe you'll join the Guild? Open a small inn?
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_11: <style=N1>Her gaze drifts off into the distance.</style> Or start a family...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_12: Just sign here. I need to return this by noon.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_15: You have your whole life ahead of you, don't throw it away! You hear me!?
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_2: <style=N1>Aunt Lori bursts into the room without knocking and slams a document on the table in front of you.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_3: I called in every favor I had to get this... Pulled every possible string.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_4: You have no idea how much it costs to bribe a royal official. <style=N1>Aunt Lori has a grim expression on her face.</style> And if the Crown ever found out...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_5: This document certifies that you have experienced a sudden and <style=E1>serious</style> breakdown in your health.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_6: Sign it, and you might just walk out of this with your head still attached.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_7: Of course, they’ll strip you of all your titles, and you’ll never be allowed to lead a caravan again...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanMid_9: You will be free to stay in the Smoldering City and pursue any other profession.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPostSeal_1: <style=N1>Aunt Lori greets you with a gentle smile, though you can see the sadness in her eyes.</style> Somehow, I always knew you’d make it, kid.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPostSeal_2: You’re just too talented for your own good... <style=N1>She shakes her head.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPostSeal_3: You should go to the Citadel. The ceremony is about to begin. The Queen's Hands are already gathering in the throne room.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPostSeal_4: This is what you wanted, right? <style=N1>Her expression is surprisingly emotionless.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPostSeal_5: Go on. You don't want to make her wait.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_1: I have spoken with your people. It seems your last caravan is ready. <style=N1>She looks at you with an expression full of sadness, but also a hint of pride.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_10: But this time, the numbers were not on our side...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_11: So there he fell, in a place without a name... <style=N1>Lori's eyes glazed over with tears.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_12: Fighting for land that would become the Crown's property in a matter of days.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_13: Killed by his soon to be allies.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_15: Oh, how I wish I could tell you that his death meant something... That he sacrificed himself for a better world...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_17: <style=N1>Lori pauses for a moment and looks at you intently, her eyes still shining with the tears she’s been holding back.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_18: Will you also die for nothing?
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_3: Have I ever told you how I lost my husband?
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_5: It was the last days of the Great Civil War... Our emissaries were "negotiating" a truce in a place that would soon become this city.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_6: He was a sergeant in a small scouting party, sent out on a routine mission in the Marshlands.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_7: There was nothing there, just an empty forest in the middle of nowhere.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_8: Or so they thought... <style=N1>In an instant, the glee in her eyes fades, replaced by a deep sadness.</style> They stumbled upon a troop of those cursed scaly bastards.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanPreSeal_9: Normally, we’d have needed at least three men to each lizard to make it an even fight.
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_10A: Leaving the others to clean up your mess...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_10B: <style=N1>Aunt Lori's mouth moves, but you hear no sound. Her gaze, vacant and lost, wanders aimlessly along the walls as if in shock. She slowly leaves the house.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_11A: <style=N1>She rushes off, slamming the door so hard your teeth rattle.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_2: <style=N1>Suddenly, the doors slam open and Aunt Lori rushes in like a charging drainage mole.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_3: Do you have <style=E1>any</style> idea what you just signed!?
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_5B: <style=N1>Aunt Lori's eyes widen in anger as she mumbles something about ignorant fools under her breath.</style>
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_6: <style=E1>Why</style> did you do that when you explicitly promised not to?
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_8A: <style=N1>Aunt Lori raises her voice, practically shouting at you.</style> Of course you do!
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_8B: <style=N1>Lori's eyes bulge as she stumbles mid-sentence.</style> What...
Dialogue_Core_IronmanStart_9A: Like any snotty young Viceroy with outsized ambitions, all you can think of is a title and a purse full of Amber!
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_1: I hear you’ve already met the Batfolk. Curious, aren't they? What did you make of them?
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_3A: <style=N1>Lori nods slowly.</style> You're not wrong. They're definitely not ones for small talk.
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_3B: <style=N1>A slight smile touches Lori’s lips.</style> You still haven't had the chance to really get to know them, huh?
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_3C: Hmm, fair enough. They do come off as harsh sometimes. And it’s true — not everyone gets along with them.
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_4: They come from a very hostile and unforgiving place, so they had to adapt. They’ve lived underground for millennia.
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_5: There are legends of vast caverns deep underground — of an entire kingdom they left behind.
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_6: All because of the Sealed Ones and their minions. They were driven to the surface world, and they still harbor a bitter resentment.
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_7: Now they've joined our ranks here in the Smoldering City. They're not the easiest to get along with, admittedly, but their metallurgical prowess is invaluable.
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_8: They’re exceptional engineers, too. You've surely noticed that each of them uses mechanical arms — a clever adaptation that leaves their wings completely free."
Dialogue_Lore_Bats_9: Unlike the Harpies, they haven't lost their ability to fly. Mainly because their kind hasn't yet endured centuries of the rain’s harmful effects.
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_1: <style=N1>Lori looks more agitated than usual, her eyes gleaming with excitement.</style> Have you heard about the new strange land that has appeared just outside the city?
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_2: I've never seen fauna and flora like this before... <style=N1>She pauses for a second, lost in thought.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_3: I've heard rumors, of course… Of faraway lands, of dangerous man-eating plants, of treasures lost at sea.
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_4: My nan used to tell such stories. But they always seemed more like tales meant to capture children's imaginations rather than reality.
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_6: <style=N1>Lori smiles and nods.</style> I asked my nan the exact same question.
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_7: The Blightstorm reshapes the world to its own dark will. We are but tiny ants scurrying upon a rock in the midst of its fury, she used to say.
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_8: I'm not sure about the "will" part, but scholars agree that the Blightstorm somehow reshapes the landscape around the Citadel. Water levels rise and fall, mountains shift, rivers change course...
Dialogue_Lore_CoastalGrove_9: It's a strange world we live in.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_1: Not a story, but perhaps a cautionary tale. <style=N1>Lori glances out of the window for a moment.</style> Not so long ago, something very strange happened in the Citadel.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_10: Hmm, I see that look on your face. <style=N1>Lori frowns slightly.</style> You don't think it seems very fair?
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_12A: Yes, some would say it's too harsh... But it's also very effective. After all, the Citadel is a remarkably peaceful place, all things considered.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_12B: Indeed, there are many who share this view. But what about those who have been wrongly convicted?
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_12C: I hope so, too. The system we have certainly keeps us safe, but... we can but hope we never find ourselves on the wrong side of it.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_13: Just... please be careful, and don't do anything stupid.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_2: For some inexplicable reason, one of the new viceroys tried to break into the Queen's throne room.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_3: Thankfully, he was quickly arrested and tried. During his sentencing, the madman shouted something about a monstrosity inhabiting the city's underworld.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_4: This was a rather notorious case, so you may have heard of it. But do you know what sentence he received?
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_6A: No. Such punishments are used very rarely.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_6B: No. There are no prisons in the Smoldering City.
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_7: The most common form of punishment is exile. <style=N1>Her expression darkened slightly.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_8: Criminals are taken far from the Citadel and left to die in the wilderness. Why waste time and amber when the Blightstorm will take care of things?
Dialogue_Lore_Criminals_9: There are some stories of convicts surviving out there, or even finding a way back... but that's just absurd.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_1: You've probably already encountered Fishmen on your adventures, right?
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_3A: Oh, I think you must have. <style=N1>An amused smile appears on her face.</style> They're everywhere!
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_3B: Exactly. There isn't a Viceroy alive who hasn't run into them at least once in their career.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_3C: <style=N1>Lori raises an eyebrow in disbelief.</style> What... how? They didn't attack you?
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_4A: And even though they’re so easy to find, no one really knows anything about them.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_5A: Almost every scholar who’s tried to contact one of their tribes has met a tragic end.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_5CA: That's... unheard of. Usually, they just attack on sight. No one's been able to get close to them.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_6: Their origin and motives remain a mystery, as does their culture and language.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_7: The only thing we know about them is that they hate fire and prefer to live in wet environments. And they don't seem to mind the Blightstorm at all.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_8: They are also believed to worship the Forsaken Gods - or the Sealed Ones, as they are commonly called.
Dialogue_Lore_Fishmen_9: Better watch your back the next time you're out there. These pesky little creatures seem harmless enough, but they can cause a lot of trouble.
Dialogue_Lore_FoxesUnlocked_1: Do you know why Foxes are commonly referred to as <style=E1>the Blight-eyed folk</style>?
Dialogue_Lore_FoxesUnlocked_3B: Well... <style=N1>Lori pauses, lost in thought. Her brow furrows as she ponders.</style> Yes, you could say so.
Dialogue_Lore_FoxesUnlocked_4: It's said that they suffer from the same disease as the Harpies. Though they must have contracted it years before, as the sickness has... changed them.
Dialogue_Lore_FoxesUnlocked_5: It seems they developed a unique connection to the Blightrot... a kind of symbiosis. Hence the name.
Dialogue_Lore_FoxesUnlocked_6: For this very reason, some fear the Blight-eyed folk. And tales of their survival in the wilderness, even during the Blightstorm, don't help...
Dialogue_Lore_FoxesUnlocked_7: But the truth is - they’re on our side. And their unique understanding of the forest and the rain helps us in our fight against the Sealed Ones.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_1: I believe I spotted some Frogfolk among your last caravan. <style=N1>Lori's eyes narrow slightly, her lips curving into a faint smile.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_2: It seems the Collegium has finally accepted you. That's a good sign - Frogs rarely follow leaders who aren't their own.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_3: You'll soon understand why they're often referred to as "keepers of the stone" in ancient writings. They shape granite as if it were clay.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_4: <style=N1>She gestures broadly, vaguely pointing to her surroundings.</style> Everything you see - the entire Citadel - was built by them. Of course, it was a joint effort between all the species, but they were the main architects.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_5: Take good care of them, and they'll become a great asset on your expeditions.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_7A: They can be... demanding. <style=N1>Lori presses her lips together and raises her hand in resignation.</style> Especially when it comes to the type of roof over their heads.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_7B: <style=N1>Lori lets out a short laugh.</style> So, you’ve already tried convincing them that a wooden wall is as good as a brick one, eh?
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_8A: Forget it! Not only do they trust stone more, but they also can't live without their pools and fountains.
Dialogue_Lore_Frogs_9: That's just the way they are. You'd better get used to it. <style=N1>She sighs silently, a slight smile on her lips.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_HarpiesUnlocked_1: I hear you've gained the trust of the Flock. It must be exciting to finally be able to take Harpies with you on an expedition.
Dialogue_Lore_HarpiesUnlocked_2: But before you embark with them, there are a few things you should know.
Dialogue_Lore_HarpiesUnlocked_3: They are native to the Red Mountain - so when the Citadel was first built, their home was forcibly incorporated into the city limits.
Dialogue_Lore_HarpiesUnlocked_4: As you can imagine, this sparked a lot of conflict in the kingdom's early years, particularly between the Harpies and the Lizards, who never had much fondness for one another to begin with.
Dialogue_Lore_HarpiesUnlocked_5: It also didn't help that back then, the Harpies were battling a new and strange disease that took away their ability to fly.
Dialogue_Lore_HarpiesUnlocked_6: To this day, they still require constant treatment... <style=N1>A shadow of sorrow passes over Aunt Lori's face.</style> And it's uncertain if they will ever fully recover.
Dialogue_Lore_Hearth_1: A story you say... <style=N1>Aunt Lori seems lost in a thought for a second.</style> How about this?
Dialogue_Lore_Hearth_2: As you know, all settlements in the kingdom are built around an Ancient Hearth. The thing is, though... we don't really know much about them.
Dialogue_Lore_Hearth_3: We know that there are hundreds of them around the Smoldering City, and that they’re all incredibly old. But we don't know who built them, or why.
Dialogue_Lore_Hearth_4: They don't really look like something the Ancients would have constructed - and they definitely weren’t made by us... <style=E1>We</style> can only build a meager copy at best.
Dialogue_Lore_Hearth_5: Some claim the Hearths predate the Ancients, but that's a very bold hypothesis. However, it must be said that the carvings on them do not resemble those of any currently living species...
Dialogue_Lore_Hearth_6: Maybe they are remnants of our own distant past... From the time when we still lived in the wilderness, in harmony with nature.
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_1: Have I ever told you about the Queen's Hands?
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_3A: It's <style=E1>"a"</style> Queen's Hand, not "the" Queen's Hand. <style=N1>Lori's eyes crinkle at the corners as she smiles.</style> There are more of us.
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_3B: That's right! <style=N1>Aunt Lori's face lights up with a joyful smile.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_3C: Huh, that's weird... <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out a quiet chuckle.</style> When I was first promoted, I couldn't stop yapping about it.
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_4: The Queen's Hands are the highest-ranking viceroys in the kingdom. They are given the hardest assignments, and report directly to the queen.
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_5: Becoming a Queen's Hand is no small feat. It takes years of faithful service to the crown, as well as a display of extraordinary skills.
Dialogue_Lore_QueesHand_6: <style=N1>Aunt Lori beams with pride.</style> You're doing great so far, so who knows... maybe you too will join our ranks someday.
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_1: Tell me, how much do you know about the rain?
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_3A: By the blazing embers... <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out a deep sigh.</style> You didn't pay much attention in school, did you?
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_3B: Yes, but it's not that simple.
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_3C: Oh yes, if it wasn't for Rainpunk, we would be utterly helpless in this cruel world.
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_4: The rain, you see, is a bit of a mystery. We don't fully understand its nature, but it carries a certain charge - a spark that fuels our machines.
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_5: That spark, however, is volatile and unpredictable. It slowly changes all living organisms it comes into contact with... often in a bad way.
Dialogue_Lore_Rain_6: Add Blightrot into the mix, and you have a recipe for disaster. Our greatest technological achievement can just as soon become our downfall.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_1: Now, tell me... everyone's talking about seals and the Sealed Ones, but did anyone tell you what they really are?
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_10: It's their world. Always has been.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_3B: <style=N1>Lori raises an eyebrow at you.</style> Some days, I wonder if half the people sitting in the Svar swapped heads with a Fishman.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_3C: <style=N1>Lori studies you intently for a second.</style> Yes... there are those who believe that.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_4C: They are living both among us, and out in the wilds, protected by their masters.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_5C: They are working tirelessly towards the return of the Sealed Ones, and the end of the world as we know it. Or at least what's left of it...
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_6: You see, not long after being promoted to a Queen's Hand, I set out to learn everything there is about the enemy.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_7: From my old nan's tales to the famous Dry Tomes hidden in the Obsidian Archive, I've scoured through everything I could find on the topic.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_8: While the different sources may diverge on almost everything else, they all agree on one thing.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes1_9: The Sealed Ones are old. As old as this land itself. They were here long before the Ancients arrived, and are still here hundreds of years after they left.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_1: Remember when I told you about my findings on the Sealed Ones, kid?
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_10A: I believe... that even the Ancients, with all their might, and all their knowledge, did not know how to deal with these beings.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_10B: <style=N1>Lori's eyes widen for a split second before she burst into roaring laughter.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_11A: So, they decided to do what anyone in their position would do – leave it for future generations to figure out.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_11B: And how would you kill them? Poke them with a pickaxe?
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_12A: Given their incredible rate of technological progress, they must have imagined they would come up with a solution eventually.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_12B: No, kiddo... I admire your bravery, but there is no fight to be had here.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_13A: But there is no future generation... there is only us.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_14A: Too dumb to read the Ancient tongue, too primitive to operate their machines.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_14B: There were... incidents in the past, when Viceroys disobeyed orders to withdraw from the Sealed Forest, thinking they could still close the seal.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_15A: Left to the mercy of forces beyond our comprehension.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_16A: Like toddlers sent on a mission to deal with a Stormbird's nest.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_17: <style=N1>Lori stares through the window at the pillar of fire rising from the Citadel.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_3B: <style=N1>Lori sighs heavily.</style> Had one Sparked Ale too many in the Svar, huh?
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_4: When the Ancients first arrived, the Sealed Ones must have already inhabited this land. Maybe they were slumbering, or perhaps they coexisted in peace for a while. We can't be certain.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_5: We don't even know their true name. We refer to them as the Sealed Ones, but they must have had a different name in the ancient tongue, long before the seals even existed.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_6: One thing is certain, though. At some point, the Sealed Ones became a problem, and the Ancients decided it was time to get rid of them.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_7: For some reason, they began constructing giant chambers beneath the earth, and imprisoned the Sealed Ones there.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes2_8: And you know what I think?
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_1: After the Ancients left, we lived in harmony for a long time. No one knew what lay hidden beneath the ground.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_10: <style=N1>Lori smiles at you, but her smile does not reach her eyes.</style> But let's not talk about the Great War today. The sun is high in the sky, and it's no time for mourning.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_2: First came the nightmares. Long before any seal had actually been broken, folks told stories about... entities, whispering to them in their dreams.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_4: You know, my nan once told me that when her grandma was little, you could tell the age of other folk by the number of storms they’d seen.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_5: But then the days between storms started to become fewer and fewer.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_6: The storm itself changed into a force of destruction and mayhem. It was hard to harvest crops, or construct anything taller than a small tree.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_7: And that was when people turned against each other. Neighbor against neighbor. Brother against brother.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_8: There have always been those who spread discord among the species, but it's much easier to convince someone that their misfortune is being caused by another when hunger stares into their eyes.
Dialogue_Lore_SealedOnes3_9: In the end, for every person who died from the hunger or sickness caused by the Sealed Ones, ten more perished fighting each other.
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_1: A mutual acquaintance tells me you've made some... questionable friends lately. Crossed paths with the Syndicate, haven't you?
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_2: Be wary of them. They're helpful and friendly at first — but fail to pay them back, and the mask quickly falls away.
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_3: I'm not exactly sure how they survive as an organization. Every time the Royal Guard reins them in, they just pop up again.
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_4: Maybe there’s an unspoken agreement that allows them to operate in the Kingdom. They must have deep connections - or be useful to the Crown in some way.
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_5: No one truly knows who leads the Black Amber Syndicate. I doubt even its own members are in the loop.
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_6: Some influential Scolopendra leaders have been spotted among their ranks, so I’d assume that’s where the Syndicate got its start. But who knows?
Dialogue_Lore_Syndicate_7: <style=N1>Lori looks at you with a hint of concern in her eyes.</style> I know they might seem helpful, especially in dire situations, but... please be careful around them.
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_1: Have you ever wondered how our profession came to be?
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_2: Before all of this. <style=N1>Lori gestures broadly at her surroundings.</style> Before the kingdom, the queen, the Blightstorm... we simply lived in the wilds.
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_3: It's hard to believe, but the storm wasn't always this bad. My nan even told me stories about permanent settlements in the Marshlands!
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_4: But when things got worse, and we retreated to the Red Mountain, we had to find a way to sustain such a large population.
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_5: At first, we tried sending out small gathering parties on short expeditions... But we quickly drained the lands around the Smoldering City of all their resources.
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_6: And that's when the first Viceroys appeared - elite settlers appointed by the queen herself. <style=N1>Aunt Lori's face lights up with a proud smile.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_Viceroys_7: It wasn't easy at first... a Viceroy not coming back from an expedition was nothing unusual. But we learned a lot, and now our organization is stronger than ever.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_1: A story, you say? Let me ask you something instead.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_10: Some say that you can find hope and solidarity in desperation. I say there is only ruthlessness and bitterness.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_11: <style=N1>Lori shakes her head suddenly.</style> Ahh, but look at me rambling again, about days long past, like a fisherman's wife. Pay me no mind.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_2: <style=N1>Lori looks past you.</style> Do you ever feel like she's too harsh on us? As if she's punishing us for sins we never committed? Would we be better off without her iron grip around our throats?
Dialogue_Lore_War1_4A: I suspect there is much we do not know about her motivations...
Dialogue_Lore_War1_4B: You are not alone in this, you know. Many young viceroys quietly dream of a life without a despot ruling over them.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_5B: They are scattered and afraid, but they scheme day and night. They dream of a world without her.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_6: She was not always here. For a long, long time after the Ancients left, we lived peacefully, in balance with nature and each other.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_7: My nan spoke of her grandmother living with Harpies and Lizards under one roof. <style=E1>Harpies and Lizards</style>, mind you!
Dialogue_Lore_War1_8: But as soon as the seals started breaking, everything changed. The forest, the storm... even the rain itself turned against us.
Dialogue_Lore_War1_9: And in the end, we turned against each other.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_1: Have you heard of the Mossback family?
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_10: Just... be careful when dealing with them.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_3A: They are one of the wealthiest families in the kingdom and have their fingers in just about every organization in the Citadel.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_3B: That's right. And you probably also met her husband, Zhorg.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_4: They mostly keep to themselves, but you've probably already met Zhorg and Zhera. They're the most prominent and public faces of the family.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_4B: Most of the family members keep to themselves, but not these two. They seem to enjoy the attention.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_5: The rest of the clan is rarely seen in public. And no one even knows if their patriarch, Zehtor Mossback, is still alive.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_6: Rumor has it that he amassed his fortune through some questionable dealings at the expense of his own kin during the Great Civil War.
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_7: And don't even get me started on the accusations surrounding his son, Zhorg... <style=N1>Lori's face contorts in an unpleasant grimace.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_8: Ah, but what am I doing? Enough of this gossip. <style=N1>She smiles with slight embarrassment.</style>
Dialogue_Lore_Zhorg_9: People love spinning tales, and most of them probably aren't even true.
Dialogue_Tip_Blightrot_1: Talk of the town is that you had an unpleasant encounter with some Blightrot recently... <style=N1>A somber expression clouds Lori's face.</style>
Dialogue_Tip_Blightrot_2: I know this might not be the best time, but I wanted to share some advice with you.
Dialogue_Tip_Blightrot_3: Blightrot is treacherous. One minute everything seems fine, and the next the purple filth is covering half your settlement. <style=N1>Aunt Lori wrinkles her nose in disgust.</style>
Dialogue_Tip_Blightrot_4: Even if you use Rainpunk wisely and don't allow cysts to grow, all it takes is one unfortunate glade with an infected caravan in it...
Dialogue_Tip_Blightrot_5: That's why it's vital to always have a Blight Post at the ready. And lots and lots of Purging Fire.
Dialogue_Tip_Blightrot_6: Remember, even if the situation seems hopeless, don't give up. Each burnt cyst not only slows down the Hearth's corruption, but also reverses some of it.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_1: I couldn't help but notice that you haven't made much use of ponds in your settlements lately. Why is that?
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_3A: It's really quite simple. <style=N1>She smiles gently.</style>
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_3B: Well... <style=N1>Lori pauses for a moment.</style> It may seem that way at first, yes
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_3C: <style=N1>Lori lets out a hearty laugh.</style> Neither do I! But luckily, we don't have to do much. We just have to be patient and reap the rewards in the end.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_4A: It works just like other ways of acquiring resources. The only difference is you don't see the results immediately - it takes a bit of patience.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_4B: It's a big investment up front, but if you bide your time, the reward is well worth the wait.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_4C: Just assign a few fishermen, forget about them, and wait until they bring you a big, stinky, but valuable load of fish. <style=N1>She smiles with amusement.</style>
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_5A: Simply build a fishing hut next to a pond, assign a few fishermen, and let them do their work in peace. They'll return with their catch when the entire pond has been depleted.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_5B: Especially if you let your fishermen use bait. And even more so when you consider how valuable these aquatic resources can be.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_5C: Especially if you let your fishermen use bait. Then they can easily double their catch.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_6A: You can also instruct them to use bait, which will dramatically increase the amount of fish they catch. It's expensive, but well worth it.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_6B: Did you know, for example, that scales can be used to make metal bars? Or that algae can be ground into flour? <style=N1>Lori's smile widens. </style>.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_7A: And if you ever find yourself in desperate need of food, just tell them to reel in the catch faster. This will deplete the pond, but at least you'll have the resources you need right away.
Dialogue_Tip_Fishing_8: Give it a try. Fishing won't be the answer to all your problems, but it will definitely help in many situations.
Dialogue_Tip_MineUpgrades_1: <style=N1>A proud smile forms on Aunt Lori's face.</style> I see you got some fancy new toys from the Brass Order.
Dialogue_Tip_MineUpgrades_2: Their inventions never cease to amaze, eh?
Dialogue_Tip_MineUpgrades_3: Upgrading your mines will make your life a lot easier. You'll be able to reach deeper mining veins or even use autonomous mine cars!
Dialogue_Tip_MineUpgrades_4: Just make sure you have enough tools and building materials. Upgrades aren't cheap.
Dialogue_Tip_Services_1: I heard some murmurs that your last few settlements didn't have any service buildings. Why is that?
Dialogue_Tip_Services_3A: That's unfortunate. <style=N1>A concerned expression clouds Aunt Lori's face.</style> But don't be discouraged. Every bad streak comes to an end eventually.
Dialogue_Tip_Services_3B: Oh... <style=N1>Lori raises an eyebrow.</style> Interesting. Maybe they'll become more useful once you venture further away from the Smoldering City.
Dialogue_Tip_Services_3C: <style=N1>Aunt Lori nods.</style> Yes, sometimes there are much more important matters to take care of first.
Dialogue_Tip_Services_4: Although service buildings are costly to build and maintain, they provide a lot in return. Most importantly, they allow you to fulfill your villagers' higher needs.
Dialogue_Tip_Services_5: They can also offer some unique benefits. Take the Temple for example. The mere presence of the Holy Flame in your settlement will help you combat Hostility.
Dialogue_Tip_Services_6: <style=N1>A warm smile graces Lori's lips.</style> Keep this in mind the next time you're out there. It might prove useful.
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_1: You seem a bit tired. Things haven't been going too well for you lately, have they?
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_3B: Maybe, maybe... <style=N1>Lori stares off into the distance, lost in thought.</style> Sometimes the cards <style=E1>are</style> stacked against us.
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_4B: But if I may offer some advice - don't fixate on a preconceived plan. Adaptability is key.
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_5: <style=N1>Aunt Lori smiles softly.</style> Remember, failure is just part of the process. Keep trying, you'll get there eventually.
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_6: Make sure you always have enough houses, and stock up on complex food as soon as you can. Using cooking wisely will net you more than you invested.
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_7: Don't be afraid to venture deeper into the forest, but always be prepared for what you may encounter there.
Dialogue_Tips_LostSettlerGames_8: Oh, and one thing that helped me immensely when I was just starting out was trading. Whether it's food shortages or unexpected events, the Merchant Guild has got you covered.
Dialogue_Tips_MoveCamps_1: I watched you during your last expedition, and noticed that you didn't move your camps. Why is that?
Dialogue_Tips_MoveCamps_3A: <style=N1>Lori lets out a hearty laugh.</style> Well, they all have wheels, don't they?
Dialogue_Tips_MoveCamps_3B: Oh... <style=N1>A faint look of surprise flashes across her face.</style> Well, in that case, just remember that it's always an option.
Dialogue_Tips_MoveCamps_4A: You can freely move all your camps, so it's a good idea to place them closer to newly discovered glades. Give it a try next time you're out there.
Dialogue_Tips_MoveCamps_5: And this doesn't just apply to camps. Shelters can also be moved, but it's a bit more costly.
Dialogue_Tips_NoHearthUpgrade_1: I noticed that you don't really like upgrading your Hearths...
Dialogue_Tips_NoHearthUpgrade_2: While this may seem like unnecessary busywork, it's actually very helpful in establishing a successful settlement.
Dialogue_Tips_NoHearthUpgrade_3: The cost is minimal, and the benefits really can make a difference. Especially since you can have multiple Hearths in one town.
Dialogue_Tips_NoHearthUpgrade_4: You only need a few decorations, houses and service buildings. Give it a try - your villagers will be grateful.
Dialogue_Tips_RareTrading_1: My friends at the Merchant Guild tell me you seem uninterested in trading with them. Why is that?
Dialogue_Tips_RareTrading_3A: <style=N1>Aunt Lori bursts out in laughter.</style> Well... yes. But they are still very useful. They saved my skin countless times, that's for sure.
Dialogue_Tips_RareTrading_3B: <style=N1>Aunt Lori raises an eyebrow.</style> Huh, you’ve never heard of them? The Merchant Guild is the wealthiest organization in the kingdom.
Dialogue_Tips_RareTrading_4: Their traders supply even the most remote of settlements. You can buy everything from food to tools and blueprints from them.
Dialogue_Tips_RareTrading_5: It never hurts to just set up a Trading Post in your town. Who knows, maybe someday that one basket of food you buy from them will save someone's life.
Dialogue_Tips_TradeRoutesUnlocked_1: I see that the Guild has finally allowed you to use their trade route network. That must've cost you a fortune.
Dialogue_Tips_TradeRoutesUnlocked_2: <style=N1>A wide smile appears on Lori's face.</style> But soon you’ll be swimming in amber.
Dialogue_Tips_TradeRoutesUnlocked_3: With trade routes, you’ll be able to export goods to neighboring towns. It's all about finding the best deals, and avoiding bad investments.
Dialogue_Tips_TradeRoutesUnlocked_4: Make sure you always have enough provisions to send out a caravan, and check your neighbors' offers every season.
Dialogue_Tips_UncollectedGoals_1: My friend at the Obsidian Archive told me you haven't visited them in quite some time.
Dialogue_Tips_UncollectedGoals_2: Remember, every time you complete a deed, you have to visit the archive and collect your reward.
Dialogue_Tips_WinningStreakOnLowDifficul: I heard you’ve been doing great lately. Not much can surprise you out there...
But I wanted to ask you something. Do you ever feel... bored?
I was worried you might say that.
I know it sounds scary, but I think you should try to venture a little further from the Smoldering City. Not many are willing to attempt it, and we could really use your help out there.
There are days when you just want to relax. In the end, it's about you enjoying your time here - so don't let any fish-head like me tell you otherwise.
The truth is... when the storm hits you <style=E1>hard</style>, leaving you isolated and struggling, you discover things about yourself that you wouldn't otherwise learn.
Try it, kid. There is no point in simply re-conquering what is already in your grasp.
Dialogue_Wiki_Adapt_1: <style=N1>Aunt Lori lets out a quiet chuckle.</style> Do you now, kid?
Dialogue_Wiki_Adapt_2: I get where you're coming from. Sometimes, things seem out of our control. I felt the same way when I was just starting out.
Dialogue_Wiki_Adapt_3: But that's just part of being a cog in this giant machine. We're often dealt what seems like a bad hand, and we just have to make the best of it.
Dialogue_Wiki_Adapt_4: I'll give you the same advice my old mentor gave me - don't have your heart set on doing things in one particular way. It'll only lead to disappointment.
Dialogue_Wiki_Adapt_5: <style=N1>Aunt Lori leans forward slightly.</style> <style=E1>Adapt.</style> Improvise. Try out new strategies.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_1: Blightrot is a nasty parasite... <style=N1>Aunt Lori's face contorts in disgust.</style> A putrid growth that constantly infests our settlements.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_2: Its most common source is Rainpunk technology. Leave a Rain Engine running for too long, and you’ll see purple, toothy flowers growing all over it.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_3: And even if you're extremely careful with Rainpunk, sometimes all it takes is one unlucky find in the woods... Come across an infected caravan, and you're in trouble.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_4: The only thing you can do is build a Blight Post and stock up on Purging Fire.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_5: Unfortunately, Blightrot Cysts can't be burned immediately, as their outer shells are impenetrable to any known tool or weapon.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_6: But once they open during a storm, they are helpless. And that's where the Blight Fighters come in.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_7: Using Purging Fire, they simply burn the cysts to a crisp. <style=N1>Lori can't help but grin.</style> As if they never existed.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_8: Remember, it's important to deal with Blightrot as quickly as possible. Don't <style=E1>ever</style> think about just ignoring it. If you let it spread, it will corrupt the Ancient Hearth and kill your villagers.
Dialogue_Wiki_Blightrot_9: Trust me, you don't want to witness that...
Dialogue_Wiki_Food_1: <style=N1>Lori nods in silence.</style> It's tough out there... And that's one of the reasons why people don't want to follow new Viceroys.
Dialogue_Wiki_Food_2: You've probably already tried putting more of a focus on farming, right?
Dialogue_Wiki_Food_4A: Of course. Forgive me for even asking. <style=N1>Lori lifts the corner of her mouth in a slight smile.</style>
Dialogue_Wiki_Food_4B: <style=N1>There is a slight trace of surprise on her face.</style> Try it. Farming might not be as glamorous as treasure hunting, but it pays off in the long run.
Dialogue_Wiki_Food_5: Trading can also be a good short-term solution, but the most effective long-term strategy is complex food production.
Dialogue_Wiki_Food_6: Be it in the Bakery, Cookhouse, or Field Kitchen... you always end up with more than you started with. Even when using the worst recipes.
Dialogue_Wiki_Hostility_1: Well, Hostility... is just the consequence of our actions. It's hard to explain, but the more we exploit the forest, the angrier it gets.
Dialogue_Wiki_Hostility_2: Every new person in your settlement, every discovered glade, every year that passes... It all affects Hostility.
Dialogue_Wiki_Hostility_3: It's a force we have to constantly fight against, as it has a huge impact on both the weather, and people's well-being.
Dialogue_Wiki_Hostility_4: But there are ways of dealing with it - careful exploration, wise management of woodcutters, or simply the right cornerstones from the queen.
Dialogue_Wiki_Hostility_5: <style=N1>Lori smiles softly.</style> It will be hard at first, but you’ll find your footing eventually.
Dialogue_Wiki_MainBranch: Struggle, you say? What’s the problem, kiddo?
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_1: Now that you've obtained a permit to use Rainpunk technology in your settlements, the real fun begins.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_10: My advice? Build Blight Posts. There aren't many problems a flamethrower can't fix.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_2: Rain engines are the brainchild of the Brass Order; devices that can be installed in production buildings to boost both productivity and speed.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_3: You’ll need the right type of rainwater to power them, of course - and a lot of it! But the Brass Order came up with a solution for this too.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_4: You see, there are these things called Geyser Pumps. Nifty little inventions. If you find a geyser somewhere in the forest, you can extract huge amounts of rainwater by attaching a Geyser Pump to it.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_5: But there are also risks involved. Tell me, have you come across any Blightrot yet?
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_7A: Then you know full well the havoc it can wreak on a settlement...
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_7B: The rumors don't do it justice.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_8: The rain is both a blessing and a curse... We can't live without it, but it also corrupts every living thing it comes into contact with.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPostUnlock_9: Rain Engines accelerate this process, creating Blightrot.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_1: Rainpunk is the technology that fuels our most advanced machines and buildings.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_2: Only the most experienced Viceroys have access to it. Permission to use it can be obtained in the Obsidian Archive.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_3: Now tell me, have you used a rain collector before?
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_4B: Just because something doesn't work like you want it to doesn't mean it's useless.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_5B: You can use rain collectors to... well, collect rainwater. The type of water depends on the season. Three seasons make for three types of rainwater in total.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_6: Later on, you can use the rain to power Rain Engines, but even without them, rainwater can still be useful.
Dialogue_Wiki_RainpunkPreUnlock_7: There are multiple recipes and events which require some hefty amounts of rainwater. It's never a bad idea to keep your tanks at least half full.
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_1: Try to understand them. They follow us into harsh and inhospitable lands, far away from their families, with no guarantee of ever coming back.
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_2: The least we can do is keep them safe and try to offer them a brief respite from their worries.
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_3: I assume you already know about the various needs of the different species?
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_5A: Every species has its own preferences. If you don't give them their favorite food, or their preferred type of entertainment, they will be unhappy.
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_5B: I thought so. <style=N1>Lori smiles gently.</style> But sometimes, food and shelter aren't enough. You also have to take care of your people's higher needs.
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_6A: It’s not always possible to please everyone - but we have to try.
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_6B: Building a tavern and investing in ale production can pay off in the long run. You might even benefit from a moment of relaxation yourself. <style=N1>Lori's lips curl into an amused grin.</style>
Dialogue_Wiki_Resolve_7: There are also other ways of keeping villagers happy, such as upgrading Hearths, mitigating Hostility, or favoring one species over another. Although that last option can be a bit risky...
Dialogue_Wiki_Trade_1: Of course! <style=N1>Lori nods with a smile.</style>
Dialogue_Wiki_Trade_2: The first thing you’ll need is a Trading Post. Once it's set up, merchants will start coming to your settlement.
Dialogue_Wiki_Trade_3: You never know what they might bring, but they’ll almost always bring something useful, like food, building materials, tools, or blueprints.
Dialogue_Wiki_Trade_4: While amber is the main currency of the kingdom, we still barter in most cases. It's just more convenient to pay with the resources you've collected.
Dialogue_Wiki_Trade_5: The Guild's prices may seem a bit unfair at first, but they have to cover their travel costs somehow. Or at least, that's their official story...
Dialogue_Wiki_Trade_6: <style=N1>A hint of disgust can be seen on Lori's face.</style> Some Viceroys even believe this justifies attacking and robbing merchants... But it doesn't.
Effect_3OrderPicks_Desc: You have preferential treatment in the Queen's Court. The pool of order choices will increase by 1.
Effect_AdventofFlame_Desc: A sacred period for all members of the Church. Start with the Temple Blueprint. {0}
Effect_AlarmBells_Desc: The Brass Order's newest invention. All workers have a {0} higher chance of producing double yields for every {1} points of expected corruption per minute in the Ancient Hearth.
Effect_AllCampsUnlock_Child_Desc: Gathering speed is decreased by {0} until you use up at least {1} gathering node charges. Source: {2}.
Effect_AllCampsUnlock_Desc: A collection of architectural drafts from a very early period in the Citadel's history. Unlocks the advanced blueprints for the Foragers' Camp, Trappers' Camp, and Herbalists' Camp, but gathering speed is decreased by {0} until you use up at least {1} gathering node charges.
Effect_AmberForArcheology_Description: The Queen has decided to reward you for your exceptional achievements in science. Gain {0} for every completed stage of an archaeological discovery (excavation, conservation, reconstruction).
Effect_AmberForSeaMarrow_Desc: Some fossils contain valuable surprises. Gain {1} for every {0} produced.
Effect_AmberForWater_Desc: Apparently, amber-like crystals can be extracted from rainwater. Gain {0} every time you use {1} units of water in Rain Engines.
Effect_AmberPayment_Desc: The Crown requires you to contribute to the Royal Treasury. At the end of each Drizzle season, you will be asked to pay {1} {0} for every 3 villagers in your settlement. If you don't, 2 people will leave.
Effect_AmberPayment_Penalty_Desc: If you don't pay the tax, the Crown will recall {0} villagers back to the Citadel.
Effect_AncientTabletforEvents_Altar_Desc: Gain {0} for every {1} completed Glade Event.
Effect_AncientTabletforEvents_Desc: Gain {0} for every {1} completed Glade Events.
Effect_ArcheologyExtraBlueprint_Descript: The Queen has decided to reward you for your exceptional achievements in science. You receive an additional blueprint choice.
Effect_ArcheologyExtraCornerstone_Descri: The Queen has decided to reward you for your exceptional achievements in science. You receive an additional cornerstone choice.
Effect_AscensionHungerMultiplier_Desc: Famine outbreaks in your previous settlements have made the villagers particularly sensitive to food shortages. Every time villagers have nothing to eat during a break, they will gain two stacks of the Hunger effect instead of one.
Effect_AutomatonInAllMines_Desc: A rainpunk automaton will permanently occupy one workplace in every mine in your settlement.
Effect_AutomatonInWoodcutter_Desc: A Rainpunk Shredder will permanently occupy one workplace in every Woodcutters' Camp in the settlement. This large automaton can fell multiple trees without returning to camp. It doesn't eat, doesn't need to rest, and can't produce double yields.
Effect_Awakening_Desc: Upon awakening the Infected Mole, all dormant cysts activate and start to corrupt the Ancient Hearth. Cysts are vulnerable to Purging Fire when this effect is activated. Completing or canceling the event will not stop the corruption, and cysts will remain active until burned.
Effect_BankruptTraderPayment_Desc: The peddler is waiting for the agreed-upon sum of {1} {0}.
Effect_BatHousesUniqueBonus_Desc: In ancient times, Bats lived in vast underground halls, now overrun by the spawn of the Sealed Ones. Each time newcomers are accepted into the settlement, you gain {0} for every villager living in a house with this upgrade.
Effect_BatsBanish_Desc: Put a villager on trial and exile them ({1}).
Effect_BatsLowerFoodConsumption_Desc: Focused minds forget hunger. Villagers have a {0} chance of not consuming food during a break.
Effect_BatsResolveForDeaths_Desc: {0} Bats gain +{1} Resolve for every {2} members of other species who leave or die. One stack of Dedication is removed each time a Bat leaves or dies.
Effect_BatsShrineGlobalExtraProd_Desc: Those who remain in your settlement tremble, fearing they will be the next to be judged. The global chance of producing double yields is increased by {0}.
Effect_Biome_CaveInitialGoods_Desc: To ease the challenge of settling these harsh lands, the Crown has allocated additional resources for your caravan: {0} and {1}.
Effect_Biome_FarmsExtraProductionForFert: Farms have a {0} higher chance of producing double yields for every {1} obtained.
Effect_Biome_FasterTrade_Desc: With such a wealth of resources, trade flourishes. Every time you sell goods worth {2} Amber, traders arrive {0} quicker and trade routes become {1} faster.
Effect_Biome_GrassSpawner_Desc: The unusually soft ground in this region has been heavily worn down by rain. Naturally occurring patches of Fertile Soil cannot be found here.
Effect_BiomeEffect_BlackMarket_Desc: The Black Amber Syndicate offers its services to Viceroys ready to tap into the riches of these lands. You gain access to a new essential building: {0}.
Effect_BiomePoroProductivity_Desc: The great distance from the Citadel means that the well-being of this creature can often be the difference between life and death for the entire village. Villagers have a {0} higher chance of producing double yields.
Effect_BiomePoroResolve_Desc: Seeing this giant ball of fluff happy somehow makes the harsh reality surrounding the settlement a tiny bit easier to bear.
Effect_BlackMarketPayment_Desc: Delayed payment for goods acquired through the Black Market.
Effect_BlackMarketPaymentLeaving_Desc: The Black Amber Syndicate always collects its debts - one way or another. If you don't pay, {0} villagers will be kidnapped from your settlement.
Effect_BlazingAmber_Desc: Cursed amber crystals burn in our vaults. Hostility increases by {0} for every {1} in the settlement's Warehouse.
Effect_BlightBomb_Explosion_Desc: The Blight Bomb explosion will destroy everything within a {0} field radius.
Effect_BlightFighterSpeed_Desc: A more compact version of the famous Blight Fighter flamethrower. Blight Fighters move {0} quicker.
Effect_BlightRateforResolveReputation_Ch: Reputation from Resolve is generated {0} slower for the next {1} Reputation Points (source: {2}).
Effect_BlightRateforResolveReputation_De: A crystalline filter designed to mitigate the negative environmental impact of infused rainwater. Blightrot Cysts appear {0} slower when using rain engines, but Reputation from Resolve is generated {1} slower for the next {2} Reputation Points.
Effect_Blightrot_Desc: Pollution from industrial production feeds the growth of Blightrot Cysts. Deploy Blight Fighters to prevent your Hearths from becoming corrupted during the storm.
Effect_BlightrotCloning_Desc: Blood Flowers have a tendency to spread uncontrollably.
Effect_BlightrotedViceroyBox_Desc: At the beginning of {0} season in year {1}, a mysterious box will arrive in your settlement.
Effect_BlightrotedViceroyBox_Pack_Desc: Your thoughts wander for a moment as you open the box.
Effect_BlightrotHigh_Desc: The Blightrot's impact is significantly stronger. Cyst generation rate is increased by +150%, while the Hearth corrupts +100% quicker than normal.
Effect_BlightrotHighDifficulty_ShortDesc: Blightrot has a significantly greater impact.
Effect_BlightrotMedium_Desc: The Blightrot's impact is stronger. Cyst generation rate is increased by +100%, the Hearth corrupts +50% quicker than normal, and all effects that spawn Blightrot now add twice as many Cysts.
Effect_BlightrotResolve_Desc: The odor of Blood Flowers is making people feel sick.
Effect_BoxCrib_Desc: Miners have found a collapsed tunnel that leads to more mining veins: {0}.
Effect_BoxCrib_StaticDesc: Miners have found a collapsed tunnel that leads to more mining veins.
Effect_BrassOrderEngineersPayment_Desc: The airship crew is waiting for your delivery of {1} {0}.
Effect_BuildingAndPacksProductionHalved_: Recipes producing building materials and packs of goods give {0} less yield.
Effect_BuriedRiches_Desc: What was once taken must now be given back. All stored <sprite name="[valuable] amber"> Amber and <sprite name="[needs] wine"> Wine will be lost.
Effect_CallTrader_Random_Desc: Summons a random trader to your settlement. If used while another trader is present, the current one will depart.
Effect_CallTrader_Syndicate_Desc: A trader from the Black Amber Syndicate will visit your settlement, offering a variety of goods for sale - like clothing, cooked food, service goods, fuel, containers, metal, wildfire essence, blueprints, and perks.
Effect_CalmLands_Desc: The forest seems to have been soothed. Opening glades no longer increases Hostility.
Effect_CaptainCurse_Desc: The captain is the last to leave the ship. Destroys a random annual Cornerstone in your possession.
Effect_CaravanProd_Desc: Discovering the remains of a caravan has caused unrest in the settlement. All villagers have a {0} chance of destroying a production yield.

Effect_CarryMoreForTablets_Desc: Stone tablets reveal the secrets of the ancients' strength. Scouts can carry {0} additional items and move {3} faster for every {1} {2} in the settlement's Warehouses.
Effect_CauldronResolve_Desc: Food tastes terrible due to contaminants from a leaking cauldron.
Effect_ChestPlunder_Desc: The convicts will not dare to attack your settlement, but they will loot whatever they can find in the forest. They destroy {0} random caches, prioritizing the ones in already discovered glades.
Effect_CloakedWandererVengeance_Desc: At the beginning of year {0}, the Cloaked Wanderer will have his revenge, killing {1} villagers.
Effect_CoalForCysts_Desc: Gain {1} for every {0} burned Blightrot Cysts.
Effect_ColdFlame_Desc: A blinding light is aimed directly at the settlement's Hearths, turning the Holy Fire into a cold flame. Hostility is increased by {0} for each Firekeeper in the settlement.
Effect_ConstructionCostForNodes_Desc: All buildings cost {0} less, but every newly discovered resource node has {1} fewer charges.
Effect_ConvictsResolve_Desc: Villagers have heard rumors of dangerous fugitives in the area. They are worried that desperate criminals might attack them.
Effect_CornerstonesLimit_Npc_Dialogue: "The laws of this place are clear, Viceroy. To claim a new cornerstone, you must first give up one you already possess. Balance must be maintained."
Effect_CorruptedSacrifice_Desc: An ancient jewel shimmers, revealing a glimmer of a faint underwater landscape. At the start of each Storm, if you have at least {1} points of expected corruption per minute, gain a permanent {0} bonus to the burning time of resources sacrificed in the Ancient Hearth.
Effect_CorruptionKill_Desc: The corruption weakens the Holy Flame's protective power and faint whispers from beyond turn into terrifying screams. Kills 3 random villagers.
Effect_CrumblingSeal_Desc: One of the seals is loosening its grip, leaking darkness upon this land. {0} season lasts {1} longer.
Effect_CystForFood_Desc: The Blightrot inside the Rainpunk Cauldron feeds on everything it encounters. For every {0} food produced, {1} Blightrot Cysts are spawned in the settlement.
Effect_CystForGlade_Desc: Trees communicate with each other through their roots, making the forest aware of your every move. Spawns {0} Blightrot Cysts every {2} seconds for every {1} Dangerous (<sprite name="dangerous">) or Forbidden Glade (<sprite name="forbidden">) discovered.
Effect_CystForHostility_Desc: The forest is merciless to those who exploit it. To protect itself, it may even sometimes ally with the Blightrot. Every {0} seconds, Blightrot Cysts ({1}) are spawned for each earned Hostility level.
Effect_CystsSpawn_Description: Large swarms of Blightrot migrate across the realm. Every third Clearance season, {0} Blightrot Cysts will appear in the settlement.
Effect_CystsSpawn_ShortDescription: Blightrot appears every third Clearance season.
Effect_DarkGateKill_Desc: Old tales talk of horrific, bloodthirsty apparitions emerging from beyond Dark Gates. Kills 10 random villagers.
Effect_DarkGateResolve_Desc: The mere presence of a Dark Gate makes the villagers fear for their lives.
Effect_DarkMist_Desc: A dark mist shrouds the menacing forest. Hostility from opened Dangerous Glades (<sprite name="dangerous">) is increased by {0}.
Effect_DepositsCharges_DefaultNestedDesc: +{0} charges to small gathering nodes, +{1} charges to large gathering nodes
Effect_DepositsCharges_NestedDescription: {0} charges to small gathering nodes, {1} charges to large gathering nodes
Effect_Desecrator_Desc: Gain {0} Hostility (Hostility scales based on difficulty). For every {1} seconds spent sacrificing goods in the Ancient Hearth, a villager dies. Sacrificing multiple resources at the same time will progress this effect's timer faster.
Effect_Disgrace_Desc: Somewhat... “unorthodox” culinary practices in one of your previous settlements have been brought to the Queen's attention. Start with {0} Impatience.
Effect_Effect_AdditionalImpatienceForDea: For the Queen, nothing is more important than her people. Losing villagers will add {0} more points to her Impatience.
Effect_EffectiveParasite_Desc: The Blightrot feeds on the tree's valuable nutrients, making new cysts much more resilient. Cysts burn for {0} seconds longer.
Effect_EggsForCysts_Desc: Blightrot spores aren't technically eggs, but they taste the same. You gain {0} when a Blightrot Cyst appears in your settlement.
Effect_EmbraceTheNight_Desc: The settlement is slowly engulfed in darkness. Each Blightrot Cyst increases Hostility by {0} points during the storm.
Effect_EngineCorrosion_Desc: Contaminated liquid gets inside Rain Engines through underground pipes. Using water in Rain Engines generates Blightrot Cysts {0} quicker.
Effect_Escape_Desc: When the specified time is up, the Treasure Stag will disappear into the forest.
Effect_EventTimeReduction10_Desc: A necklace made out of tiny bones. Scouts work {0} faster on Glade Events.
Effect_ExplorationTax_Desc: Taking advantage of the riches of this new land will cost you. You must pay {0} <sprite name="[valuable] amber"> Amber every time you discover a Small Glade, and {1} <sprite name="[valuable] amber"> Amber every time you discover a Dangerous (<sprite name="dangerous">) or Forbidden Glade (<sprite name="forbidden">) . Otherwise, 2 villagers will be recalled to the Citadel.
Effect_ExplorationTaxPayment_Big_Desc: You discovered a Dangerous (<sprite name="dangerous">) or Forbidden Glade (<sprite name="forbidden">). The Crown requires you to pay {1} {0}.
Effect_ExplorationTaxPayment_Small_Desc: You discovered a small glade. The Crown requires you to pay {1} {0}.
Effect_ExtendTradeRoutes_Description: Each neighboring town offers {0} additional Trade Route option(s)
Effect_Extractor_WaterPerMinAndTank_Desc: {0} Increases the tank capacity for every type of rainwater by {1}.
Effect_ExtraProdForConsumption_Desc: All workers have a {0} higher chance of producing double yields, but they also have a {1} higher chance of consuming twice as much food during a break.
Effect_ExtraProductionForCorruption_Desc: It was not you who removed this fragment, weakening the ancient seal - but you would still be executed on the spot if someone was to find it in your possession. Effect_ExtraProductionForRelicsInProgres: The courage and hard work of the town's scouts mobilizes other workers to be more productive. All workers get a {0} higher chance of doubling their production for every Dangerous Glade Event that is being worked on.
Effect_ExtraProductionForRelicsResolved_: Archaeologists have learned a lot about a long-lost culture by examining old ruins. All workers get a {0} higher chance of producing double yields for every {1} completed Dangerous and Forbidden Glade Events.
Effect_ExtraTraderMerch_Altar_Desc: Traders offer 1 additional perk or blueprint. You also gain an Active Ability that summons a trader to your settlement. This ability can be used from the Main Warehouse and has 5 uses.
Effect_ExtraTraderMerch_Desc: Traders will have 1 more perk or blueprint for sale.
Effect_FallenViceroyCommemoration_Desc: Villagers with their need for species-specific housing met will get an additional +2 to Resolve.
Effect_FamiliesGratitude_Desc: Relatives of your villagers send gifts for treating their family members well. Get {0} for every full Reputation Point obtained through high Resolve.
Effect_FasterCorruption_Desc: Your settlement's strongest and weakest point has become a direct target for the Blightrot. Corruption in the Ancient Hearth grows {0} quicker.

Effect_FasterLeaving_Desc: Villagers are less understanding than they used to be. They’re probably getting a bit spoiled by now. Villagers are {0} faster to leave if they have low Resolve.

Effect_FedoraHat_Desc: An old inscription on the bottom of the hat says: "Fortune and glory". Increases the chance of doubling event loot by {0} (this doesn't apply to perks and blueprints).
Effect_FewerBlueprintsOptions_Desc: The greedy Royal Archivist sold most of the blueprints to traders and fled the Citadel. You have {0} fewer blueprint choices. You can gain an additional choice by spending <sprite name="[valuable] ancient tablet"> Ancient Tablets.
Effect_FewerCornerstonesOptions_Desc: The Royal Envoy comes to you with bad news. The Queen has restricted your cornerstone choices by {0}. You can gain an additional choice by spending <sprite name="hearth parts"> Wildfire Essence.
Effect_FewerInitialBlueprints_Desc: The Queen has visited the Obsidian Archives in person, and was dissatisfied with the amount of funding spent on expeditions. You have one fewer initial blueprint.
Effect_FewerInitialBlueprints_ShortDesc: One fewer blueprint to begin with.
Effect_FirstElderCat_Desc: From time to time, a weary villager stops to pet the cat, finding comfort in the reminder of their true home on the slopes of Red Mountain.
Effect_FishingSpeed_Desc: More durable and much wider nets. Fishing speed is increased by {0}.
Effect_FishmenFoodPoison_Desc: Fishmen are small and cunning enough to sneak into a settlement and poison the food supply. Villagers have a {0} chance of death after eating.

Effect_FishmenOutpostResolve_Desc: Something is observing the villagers from the edge of the woods.
Effect_FishmenOutpostResolve_Hooked_Desc: With each fallen tree, the Fishmen grow closer. Global Resolve is hit by a {0} penalty for every {1} fallen trees.
Effect_FishmenSoothsayerCurse_Desc: The comforts of the civilized world are disgustingly unnatural to the Fishmen. Every time {0} Complex Food, Clothing, or Service needs are fulfilled, {1} random villagers are killed.

Effect_FishmenWitchcraft_Desc: Fishmen witches have prepared a special surprise for anyone trying to break into the cave. Spawns {0} Fishmen Totems.
Effect_FoodProductionSpeed20_Desc: A handy set of notes on how to survive in the wilderness, written by an anonymous viceroy. Increases global food production speed by {0}.
Effect_FoodProductionSpeed50_Desc: All food production (both raw and cooked) is {0} slower.
Effect_ForbiddenforHostility_Desc: Securing the deadliest corners of the forest will make it a lot less terrifying. Effect_FrogForUpgrade_Desc: Members of the Frog clan flock to your settlement. Gain {0} Frog villager for every {1} house upgrades.
Effect_FrogGracePeriod_Ability_Desc: Removes {0} Impatience Point, but after one season, you must pay the Crown {1} <sprite name="[valuable] amber"> Amber. Otherwise, you'll gain {2} Impatience Points.
