Wiki_Blightrot_Content:
Blightrot is a dangerous parasite that can infect buildings in your settlement. The most common source of Blightrot is Rainpunk technology - a side effect of using Rain Engines in your production buildings (you can read more in the "Rainpunk" entry in the Encyclopedia). However, you may also encounter Blightrot in the wild - in Glade Events or Forest Mysteries.
 
Blightrot accumulates gradually over time. When it reaches a certain threshold, Blightrot Cysts will begin to appear on buildings. Each building can have a maximum of three Blightrot Cysts. Once this limit has been reached, Blightrot will start spreading to nearby buildings.
 
At first, Blightrot Cysts remain dormant, but during storm season, they awaken and begin corrupting the Ancient Hearth (indicated by a progress bar above the Hearth and in the Hearth's UI when selected). Once the progress bar reaches the end, a negative effect will trigger, killing a number of your villagers. The more active Blightrot Cysts there are, the faster the corruption progresses.
 
To combat the spread of Blightrot, you need to build Blight Posts and create a resource called Purging Fire. Blightrot Cysts are invulnerable for most of the year, but during storm season, they open and become vulnerable. This is when Blight Fighters can go around the settlement and burn them down. Removing a cyst will not only slow down the corruption process, but will also remove some of the accumulated corruption from the Hearth.
 
The Ancient Hearth can also be reinforced by building and upgrading other smaller Hearths in your settlement.
Wiki_BuildingMaterials_Content:
There are three types of refined building materials: Planks (made from wood), bricks (made from clay or stone), and fabric (made from plant fiber, algae, or reeds). Almost all complex buildings (aside from camps or shelters) require these for construction. You'll always have access to the Crude Workstation, where you can craft building materials, but there are also other buildings in the game that can make them a lot faster, and with fewer resources needed.
 
There is also one special type of building material that’s used for constructing camps and some production buildings: parts. Parts are a rare resource that can only be acquired through orders, exploration, or trading. 
 
All building materials will be refunded when you demolish a constructed building. To destroy a building, select the “destroy” tool.
Wiki_ConsumptionControl_Content:
You can control what your villagers are allowed to eat and which needs they can fulfill using the Consumption Control Panel. To open the panel, select the Consumption Control icon on the upper right corner of the screen. There you can use the checkboxes assigned to each species and item to customize what is being consumed, and what is forbidden. 

Villagers can get upset and suffer a Resolve penalty if they are forbidden from consuming goods that are available in the settlement's Warehouses. This penalty will be even higher if another species is allowed to consume said goods. Penalties vary between different types of resources. The only exception is raw food (such as mushrooms or roots), which will never activate any penalties.
Wiki_Cycle_Content:
The world of Against the Storm is governed by an eternal Cycle. Every few decades, a cataclysm known as the Blightstorm wipes out the entire World Map. The only safe haven is the Smoldering City. 

The calendar at the bottom of the screen shows how much time is left until the next Blightstorm. The bar slowly fills up with each settlement you complete or abandon. The amount of time is based on the number of years you spend in a given town. 

When the bar at the bottom of the screen fills up, you will no longer be able to build new settlements. You can only complete the cycle by pressing the highlighted button next to the calendar. 

Once the Blightstorm begins, the World Map will begin to reshape itself. Settlements are destroyed, biomes regenerate, and modifiers appear in new locations.
Wiki_Events_Content:
Glade Events are objects found in the forest, like abandoned caches, survivor camps, ruins, wild beasts, etc. Some of them are positive, offering goods or new villagers in exchange for a small amount of resources. Others are dangerous, forcing you to act quickly to avoid negative consequences (while also giving you generous rewards should you complete them).
 
Once you select a Glade Event, the Event Panel will appear. There you'll be able to find a few different sections: effects, worker slots, requirements, and rewards. The effect section shows you the possible negative consequences of the event, and how much time you have left before they occur. To complete an event, you need to assign workers to it, choose one of two options (if the event has more than one solution), and select “investigate”. 
 
Very often, events have more than one way of being solved. Most events offer two different approaches, with each approach having its own requirements, rewards, and so called "working effects".
 
Working effects are special conditions that activate once you give the order to investigate an event (like a Resolve penalty, a slow debuff, etc.). Your goal is to survive these conditions for a set amount of time. After an event has been completed, your workers will deliver the rewards to your Warehouse, and no negative effects will trigger.
Wiki_Exploration_Content:
Although you’re surrounded almost entirely by a thick forest, there are smaller and bigger glades around your starting location. To establish a successful settlement, you’ll have to cut your way through to them. Glades can contain resources, treasures, fertile soil, ruined buildings, and more. Use the tree marking tool (the axe icons on the right hand side of the lower central HUD) to point your woodcutters to specific areas of the forest they should prioritize.

The best rewards come from Dangerous or Forbidden Glades (marked with a skull icon), but these always have at least one Dangerous Glade Event within them, which will require you to deliver certain goods, or complete a challenge to complete them.
Wiki_FactionsAndInfluence_Content:
There are multiple competing factions constantly trying to settle the World Map. It usually takes them a few years to establish a town - but if they succeeded, they’ll claim the resources of surrounding map tiles and remove any nearby modifiers or treasure chests. Once a faction decides where to settle, a colored border with a number will appear on a given map tile. The number shows how many years are left before the faction establishes the town.

Although faction towns may sometimes be an obstacle in your endeavors, they can also be very useful. If you have a Trading Post in your settlement, and a faction town is located nearby, you can establish trade routes with it. 

With every action you take on the World Map (establishing towns, collecting treasure, removing modifiers, etc), you’ll gain Influence. At the end of each cycle, you’ll be ranked based on said influence, and compared to other factions. The higher you place in the ranking, the higher the reward you’ll receive from the Queen.
Wiki_Farming_Content:
To start farming, you’ll need a farm building (like the Small Farm, Forester's Hut, Herb Garden, or Plantation) with some farm fields nearby, which can only be placed on fertile soil. Plants will be sowed only during drizzle season, and harvested only during clearance. If crops are not harvested before the storm, they will wither. You can change the plants you want to sow by selecting the farm and choosing the checkbox next to the desired crop’s icon.

If you leave workers assigned to the farm during the storm, they will plow the farm fields, adding an extra chance for double yields next year.
Wiki_Fishing_Content: Fishing is similar to gathering but is considered a separate resource acquiring method, especially when considering perks and orders (much like mining and farming). To start fishing, you need a Fishing Hut (a small version is always available) and a pond (which can be found in glades). Place the Fishing Hut near the pond and assign workers. Unlike regular gatherers, fishermen catch fish and algae in nets at the pond. They only transport resources to the warehouse once the entire pond is depleted. Resources in nets can't be used for production or consumption until they are moved to the warehouse. If you need the resources sooner, you can deplete the pond by selecting it and using the "Retrieve Nets" button. Ground bait can double the yield from fishing. To use bait, select the Fishing Hut and choose one of three options: - None - where no bait is used - Optional - where bait is used if available - Only With Bait - where fishing occurs only when bait is available. Ground bait is made from Packs of Crops at the Fishing Hut. Fishermen take it from your warehouse, convert it into bait, and then use it at the pond. One piece of bait boosts one production cycle at the pond.
Wiki_Food_Content:
Your villagers need to eat in order to survive. Every few minutes, they will go on a break, gather around the Hearth, and try to get something edible from the Warehouse. If nothing they like is available (like pickled goods for Beavers), they will eat raw food. If there is no food whatsoever, villagers will get one stack of the ‘Hunger’ effect. Each stack works as a Resolve penalty, and if the Resolve of a species reaches 0, they will start leaving the settlement.

Each species can only withstand a certain number of 'Hunger' stacks before dying of starvation. To see the exact number of stacks a species can survive, go to the "species" section in the Encyclopedia, and look for the "Hunger Tolerance" attribute. For example, a Human has a Hunger Tolerance of 6, which means they will die after seven breaks in a row without consuming any food.

Even if you grow vegetables on your farms, the amount of food you produce will soon become insufficient for a growing population. The solution is to process raw food and thus multiply it, as most recipes yield more goods than the raw ingredients used to produce them. Some perks can further increase that ratio, or even generate additional food as a byproduct.
Wiki_Hearth_Content: The Hearth is crucial to the survival of your village. If the fire goes out, people's Resolve will start falling drastically. To keep the flame burning, a firekeeper and a steady supply of fuel (like wood, sea marrow, coal, or oil) are needed. You can decide which types of fuel will be burned in the Hearth by selecting it and using the checkboxes next to the relevant fuel types in the building’s UI.
Wiki_Hostility_Content:
You start each settlement with the Hostility of the forest at level 0. As your town grows, this Hostility will slowly increase when you perform certain actions, like discovering glades, welcoming new villagers, or assigning new woodcutters (you can find the full list of Hostility sources by hovering over the Hostility icon). Some actions can lower the Hostility of the Forest - like building additional Hearths, or letting the Queen’s Impatience grow. With each Hostility level, a negative Resolve penalty is applied to all villagers, and new forest mysteries can become active. 

Forest mysteries are generated at the start of each game, based on the map’s difficulty and biome. Each effect is only active during its corresponding season. Positive effects occur during drizzle, while negative ones are active during the storm. Some effects are simple modifiers that influence production, reduce speed or destroy buildings, but some are based on your villagers' needs. For example: Hailstorm can kill villagers during the storm - but if they have a home, they’ll be safe.
Wiki_Hubs_Content:
When expanding your settlement, it’s very useful to set up hubs in far-away glades, so that your villagers don't have to walk all the way back to the town center just to deposit collected goods or take a break. To create a hub, you'll need to build a Warehouse and a Small Hearth (and assign a new firekeeper). You can have multiple hubs at once - if, of course, you can afford to build them and have enough fuel to sustain multiple Hearths. It's also important to remember that each Hearth has its own range, and can't be placed too close to other Hearths (their area of effect can't overlap). 
 
Hearths can be upgraded by building homes, decorations, and service buildings within their range. Each Hearth level will grant you bonuses to Resolve, production speed, and production output. These bonuses stack with each Hearth in your settlement.
Wiki_Logistics_Content:
Every building has its own internal storage, where the goods it produces or gathers are temporarily stored. When the internal storage reaches its limit, the goods in it will be transported to the Main Warehouse by a worker. While transporting, it’s important to keep in mind that villagers have a limited carry capacity (depending on their profession and active perks), so they might need to walk between their workplace and the Main Warehouse multiple times. 
 
Goods kept in a building’s internal storage can also be accessed by workers from other production buildings (as ingredients for recipes they’re working on). If two buildings are close enough and use each other's internal storage, an animated dotted line will be visible between them (after selecting one of the buildings).
 
Sometimes deliveries and production might stall for a while because of breaks. Every few minutes, workers will return to a nearby hearth to eat and rest. During a break, they'll consume at least one item of food and try to fulfill all their needs (clothing, services). If a villager has multiple needs tied to complex food, they will consume more than one meal.
Wiki_Modifiers_Content:
The World Map is full of things waiting to be discovered. Every point of interest on the map is marked with a question mark and may turn out to be either a modifier or a World Event. 

Modifiers are special types of objects that change the rules of the game (for example, by allowing you to move any building in your settlement, or by blocking your ability to trade). To accept a modifier challenge, simply settle on a map tile adjacent to it. After you win a game near it, the Modifier will disappear and you'll be rewarded with additional Citadel Resources or, in some cases, a special Supply Box from the Queen herself (with unique rewards such as Seal Fragments or Reserve Embarkation Points).

World Events, on the other hand, are short, random encounters that offer a specific choice or challenge. To interact with an event, simply select it when it's in range (events are indicated by an exclamation point). A dialog box will appear with several options to choose from - some are as simple as giving up a villager from the caravan for additional resources in each subsequent game, while others require you to win a run under certain conditions.
Wiki_Prestige_Content:
Prestige is a special difficulty scaling system that offers increasing challenges and rewards. There are a total of 20 levels of prestige in Against the Storm, and in order to reach the next rungs on the difficulty ladder, you must first win at least one game at a lower level. Each prestige level adds one new negative effect to the pool of modifiers with which you start the game. This means that by reaching prestige 20, you will face as many as 20 negative modifiers (plus all the variables resulting from non-prestige difficulty levels, such as storm length, Hostility multipliers, etc.).

To help you in this extremely difficult endeavor, you have a special new building at your disposal - the Forsaken Altar. With it, you can buy extremely powerful, Stormforged versions of Cornerstones, as well as upgrade some of your already-owned perks to this mythical rarity.

To use the Forsaken Altar, you must first earn enough Reputation points. The points thresholds that activate the Forsaken Altar are indicated on the reputation bar by small red dots. Once you have reached the appropriate threshold, you still have to wait for the Storm to start, as the creature that inhabits the Altar will not want to come out in any other season.

Once all of the above conditions are met, you will finally be able to use the Altar. Every altar activation allows you to select one of three Stormforged Cornerstones. You can only choose one of them, and you must pay for it with Citadel Resources and the lives of some of your subjects. Note that some Cornerstones are cheaper than others because you are not buying them, but rather upgrading a perk you already possess (the text on the purchase button will change to “upgrade” in that case).
Wiki_Rainpunk_Content:
Rainpunk technology utilizes the unique properties of the rain to power advanced machinery. You can harness this technology by installing Rain Engines in your production buildings, and fueling them with Infused Rainwater. Rain Engines can increase production speed, improve the chance of additional yields, and reduce the workload on workers.
 
To install Rain Engines, select a production building and navigate to the Rainpunk tab. These engines require pipes for installation, and need to be fueled with rainwater to operate. Once installed, you can adjust their power levels, monitor their water consumption, and see the speed at which pollution (Blightrot) is generated.
 
There are three types of infused rainwater: drizzle water (green), clearance water (yellow), and storm water (blue). These can be collected from Geysers found in glades, or by using a Rain Collector. Each Geyser contains only one type of water, and a Geyser Pump must be built on top of the Geyser to extract it. Rain Collectors gather rainwater based on the current season.
 
Different buildings require different types of water. Drizzle water is primarily used in food production, clearance water is for crafting and artisanry, while storm water is used to boost heavy industrial production.
 
On difficulty levels higher than Pioneer, using Rain Engines to boost production will result in the growth of a parasite known as Blightrot. The more infused rainwater is used in a production building, the faster Blightrot Cysts will appear on it (and eventually spread across the settlement). For more information on Blightrot, refer to the "Blightrot & Corruption" entry in this Encyclopedia.

Unlock Rain Engines by buying the Obsidian Archive Level 6 upgrade in the Smoldering City.
Wiki_Rainpunk_Content_Addon: Unlock Rain Engines by buying the Obsidian Archive Level 6 upgrade in the Smoldering City.
Wiki_Recipes_Content: You can customize the recipes used in your production buildings, deciding what to make, what ingredients to use, and how many to make. To do this, select a building or use the Recipe Panel (the "book" icon in the top right corner of the HUD). To enable or disable a recipe for a specific resource, select the checkbox next to its icon. To change the ingredients used, select a resource in the recipe and choose a substitute from the radial menu. To set a production limit, use the horizontal bar in the Limit section, or enter a number in the text box.
Wiki_Reputation_Content:
You can gain Reputation Points in three different ways: 
 - by successfully completing orders, 
 - by exploring your surroundings, 
 - or by keeping your villagers happy. 

Orders are very straightforward - you always get at least 1 Reputation Point for completing them. To gain Reputation for villagers’ well-being, you have to increase their Resolve so that it reaches the Reputation Threshold (indicated by a blue line on the resolve bar). After that, they will start generating Reputation Points passively. 

With time, your villagers will become accustomed to their living conditions, and the reputation threshold will increase, forcing you to satisfy more complex needs.

To acquire Reputation from exploring, you will have to cut your way through the forest to Dangerous or Forbidden Glades, and complete the glade events located there. But beware, these events can be challenging at times - or might require you to deliver special resources to complete them.

Some perks or goods bought from traders can also increase your Reputation.
Wiki_Resolve_Content:
Resolve is the main indicator of your villagers’ well-being. It’s represented by a number between 0 and 50, and is calculated for each species based on its Base Resolve and all positive and negative effects influencing it. For example: with 10 Base Resolve, Beavers under the influence of the effect “Beaver Clan Support” (+3 to Beaver Resolve) will end up with 13 Resolve. As long as it’s above 0, they won't leave your settlement. 

To increase Resolve, you have to satisfy your villagers’ needs - by giving them complex food (like jerky, pie, etc.), clothing (coats, boots), or access to services (like a tavern serving ale). Resolve will grow gradually, and at a different rate for each species. To see the exact Resolve change, open the Species Panel using the arrow key next to the species’ portrait, and hover over the numbers shown next to the species’ name. There you will find the Current Resolve and Future Resolve. 

Current Resolve reflects the Resolve a given species currently has, while Future Resolve is the sum of all effects – in other words, the value that the Current Resolve will eventually reach over time.

Raising Resolve to an exceptionally high level (indicated by the blue line on the resolve bar) will generate Reputation Points passively. However, this won't last indefinitely, as villagers will get used to their standard of living with each point acquired, and the blue line on the Resolve bar will move further up.
Wiki_Sacrificing_Content:
During especially hard times, you can sacrifice additional goods in the Hearth to temporarily gain positive effects. Each fuel type grants different boons, like increasing your production speed, decreasing Hostility, etc. To do this, select the Hearth, navigate to the Sacrifice Panel, and choose the resource you want to burn. The selected goods will be taken from your warehouse at a rate of one every few seconds. You can control how much will be consumed by using the arrow buttons. The more you sacrifice, the stronger a given bonus becomes.

Sacrificing consumes resources at a very high rate, and might drain your storage very quickly. Always remember to turn it off when you no longer need it.
Wiki_Seals_Content:
The Blightstorm Cycle is said to be somehow connected to the strange ancient seals found all around the World Map. These intricate structures were built by a long-forgotten civilization, and it is believed that they hold a primeval, malevolent force at bay - the so-called Sealed Ones.

Unfortunately, the power of the seals has gradually waned over the millennia, causing the Sealed Ones to slowly regain their hold on this world. Your goal as the Queen’s Viceroy isn’t just to establish settlements and collect resources, but also to reforge these ancient seals and help the Crown protect the kingdom.

To reforge a seal, you will have to journey toward it with your caravan, collect enough seal fragments on the way there (by winning games and completing modifiers), and successfully settle right next to it at the very end of the cycle. If you make it there much sooner, you can try and reforge it right away, but the cycle will end as soon as you start your settlement in the Sealed Forest.

There are several types of seals with distinct names and symbols. Each subsequent seal requires more seal fragments and is located further away from the Smoldering City. At the beginning of your journey, you will only see four seals on the World Map (two of the same type as the recently completed one, and two new ones). But once you reforge the Gold Seal for the first time, you will gain access to Seal Contracts - a feature that allows you to freely pick which types of seals will spawn on the World Map.

Successfully reforging a seal will grant you additional Citadel Resources at the end of the cycle. The first time that you reforge a specific seal type, the time between future Blightstorms will be extended by a few years.
Wiki_Services_Content:
Villagers fulfill their most basic needs, such as food or clothing, at the Hearth, and need only the right goods to do so. However, there is a separate category of needs that require not only resources, but also a special type of building to fulfill them. These are called "services."
 
Services needs include things like Leisure, Luxury, or Religion. To fulfill them, the village will need a suitable service building, such as a Tavern or a Market. Once the appropriate building has been built, workers must be assigned to it. They will then take goods from the Warehouse, bring them back to their workplace, and serve them to residents.
 
Villagers don't have to physically go to a service building to fulfill their service needs. They will still rest at the Hearth as usual, but for them to fulfill the need for Leisure, a Tavern must be present and operating somewhere in the settlement.
 
Service buildings also offer unique passive bonuses. These are usually global positive effects that activate when a building has a certain number of employees. For example, having 3 workers assigned to the Tavern increases Resolve for all villagers in the settlement. However, passive service building bonuses don't stack, so building a second Tavern will not double this effect.

Wiki_TradeRoutes_Content:
Once you have a Trading Post in your settlement, you can access trade routes. They allow you to export goods to other nearby settlements in exchange for the main currency of the realm - Amber. You can open the Trade Route Panel by selecting the icon in the top right corner of the screen. 

In the Trade Route Panel, you can see the goods your nearest neighbors are willing to buy from you. These are called offers. Offers change with each season, and depend on the biome in which a settlement has been constructed. There are three main parameters to keep in mind: payment (how much the settlement is willing to pay), travel cost (how much it will cost to send a convoy), and travel time (how long it will take to traverse the trade route). You can use the up and down arrow buttons next to an offer to change its multiplier and increase the amount of goods traded in a given transaction. 

After accepting an offer, the chosen goods will be sent to the selected town. You’ll be able to collect the Amber you’ve earned for the resources you’ve sold when the trade route's travel time expires. Each successful trade with a neighbor will increase your standing with them. The more a given settlement likes you, the better its future offers will be.
Wiki_Trading_Content:
Once you build a Trading Post, traders will visit you periodically. You can barter with them by selecting their goods and offering some of your resources in return. The bar beneath the selected goods will show you if the trader is happy with your proposal, and once the bar turns green, you can press the “trade” button to confirm the transaction.

When there’s no trader in town, you can select the Trading Post to find out when the next one arrives. Traders will not come during the storm. Traders can also be attacked and robbed. To do so, use the sword icon in the Trade Panel. But beware, this action will have severe consequences.
Wiki_Twitch_Content: Against the Storm features Twitch integration, which lets you interact with your viewers without any external software or bots. To enable it, go to the game's Options (Twitch tab), log in with your Twitch account, customize your setup, and encourage your audience to play alongside you. There are two main aspects of the integration: - Chat minigame: Forest Guardians vs. Council of Elders - Chat polls: Cornerstone, blueprint, caravan, newcomers, and order voting (requires Affiliate or Partner status) Chat polls The audience can vote for your in-game choices via native Twitch polls. You can customize the voting mode, channel points usage, and poll duration in the game's Options (Twitch tab). Currently, Chat polls support cornerstone, blueprint, caravan, newcomers, and order voting. Chat minigame: Forest Guardians vs. Council of Elders With the chat minigame enabled, randomly selected viewers (who opted into the minigame) will actively try to help you or put obstacles in your way. When the chat game is active, your audience can join one of two factions: Forest Guardians (by typing !join forest) or the Council of Elders (by typing !join town). Guardians will try to oppose your settlement, while the Council will aid you. During a run, each faction has three slots for characters, which are randomly chosen from their members (who opted in to participate). Each character can enable one of the three abilities by typing commands in the chat. The cooldown for these abilities can be adjusted in the game's Options (Twitch tab). Each viewer can be defeated, in which case they lose control over the character and their active ability is disabled. The next faction member will be selected after a cooldown. Council of Elders Viewers who join the Council have their Twitch names displayed above a villager in the settlement. Abilities: !prayer - increases the chance for double production !tale - increases the global Resolve !speech - slows the rate at which villagers leave If a villager controlled by a Council Member dies or leaves, the Council Member is defeated. Forest Guardians Viewers who join the Guardians hide in nearby Dangerous or Forbidden Glades, their Twitch usernames visible above the events in those glades. Abilities: !poison - passively removes food from the Warehouse !anger - increases the Hostility of the Forest !chant - slows down event working speed Once the dangerous event has been resolved, the Guardian will be defeated. Additional Information Viewers can type !help to get a list of commands and a short explanation. This option has a cooldown to prevent spamming. Viewers in control of Guardians or Council Members will eventually be removed after leaving the chat, but it can take up to a few minutes for Twitch to realize they’re missing. Users can type !leave to leave their faction and pick a new one, or when they no longer want to participate in the minigame. To avoid the need for any external bots, the game logs into the chat as yourself - the creator. If you have any questions, technical issues, or suggestions regarding Twitch integration, please reach out to us on our Discord server.
Wiki_WinningAndLosing_Content: In Against the Storm, you build not one, but many settlements. To successfully establish a town, and therefore win a run, you need to collect enough Reputation Points to fill the entire reputation bar (blue). It’s important to do this before the Queen’s Impatience (red) reaches its maximum. If the Queen loses her patience, you will lose. You also lose if all your villagers either leave or die.
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Desc: As you ponder your next move, a group of commoners approaches, their faces etched with worry. They tell you of their relatives stranded in a settlement abandoned by their Viceroy, who has fled, leaving them to face their fate alone. Their pleas are filled with desperation as they beg for your help.

WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option1_Tooltip: Start the game here, in a settlement founded by another viceroy (with some pre-selected blueprints, a few selected cornerstones, some discovered glades, and a partially built town). If you win, you will receive {0} for the duration of this Cycle.
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option2_Condition: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Complete a deteriorated settlement founded by another Viceroy (with some pre-selected blueprints, a few pre-selected cornerstones, some discovered glades, some badly handled events, and a partially built town).
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option2_Desc: Negotiate the reward (<color=#00D4FF>complete a deteriorated settlement</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0} and {1}</color>)
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option2_Tooltip: Start the game here, in a settlement founded by another viceroy (with some pre-selected blueprints, a few selected cornerstones, some discovered glades, some badly handled events, and a partially built town). WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option3_Condition: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Complete a deteriorated settlement founded by another Viceroy (with some pre-selected blueprints, a few pre-selected cornerstones, some discovered glades, some badly handled events, and a partially built town).
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option3_Desc: Do it for free (<color=#00D4FF>complete a deteriorated settlement</color>)
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Option3_Tooltip: Start the game here, in a settlement founded by another viceroy (with some pre-selected blueprints, a few pre-selected cornerstones, some discovered glades, some badly handled events, and a partially built town).
WorldEvent_AdoptedTown_Reward: It wasn't easy, but you did it. The villagers are grateful for your help.
WorldEvent_AdoptedTownOnlyGlades_Desc: A giant Tree Grazer recently passed through this area. You start your settlement with 2 Dangerous Glades, and 2 to 3 Small Glades already open.
WorldEvent_BankruptTrade_Option1_Desc: Agree to deliver Amber (<color=#00D4FF>deliver {0} and win before year {1} starts</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {2} villager</color>)
WorldEvent_BankruptTrade_Option1_Tooltip: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will get {1} more villager for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_BankruptTrade_Option2_Desc: Raise the stakes (<color=#00D4FF>deliver {0} and win before year {1} starts</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {2} villagers</color>)
WorldEvent_BankruptTrade_Option2_Tooltip: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will get {1} more villagers for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_BankruptTrade_Reward: The trader seems ecstatic at the sight of the Amber you brought him.
WorldEvent_BankruptTrader_Desc: Wading through the forest, you encounter a peddler pulling a wagon. It looks like his luck has run out and he's desperate to bounce back. If you bring him enough amber, he is willing to lend you some of his best workers until the end of the cycle.
WorldEvent_BlackAmberSyndicate_Desc: As your caravan creaks across a crumbling ancient bridge, a hooded figure steps into your path. An insectoid mouth clicks beneath the hood. "These are dangerous lands, stranger. Perhaps we could offer you some... help?" Before you can respond, more cloaked figures emerge from the shadows, their gazes expectant. It’s clear this isn't an offer one refuses lightly.
WorldEvent_BlackAmberSyndicate_Option1_D: Cut a deal (<color=#FF8400>become cursed for {0} games</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain access to a Syndicate Trader</color>)
WorldEvent_BlackAmberSyndicate_Option2_D: Negotiate (<color=#00FF15>traders sell mystery boxes for the next {0} games</color>)
WorldEvent_BlackAmberSyndicatePayment_De: Pay {1} {0} before year 6 starts, or 4 villagers will be kidnapped.
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Desc: As your caravan crosses one of the kingdom's many nameless rivers, you encounter a hideous creature. Were it not for the tattered remains of a viceroy's uniform, you might mistake it for another child of the forest. Afflicted with Blightrot, it must have been cast out by its own people. It shuffles slowly toward you, begging for the chance to serve its beloved Queen one last time.
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Option1_Co: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Win a game with the Blight-Ridden Viceroy effect ({0} Blightrot Cysts appear with every {1} raw or complex food produced).
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Option1_De: Accept its help (<color=#00D4FF>win despite spreading Blightrot</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0}</color>)
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Option1_To: Win a game with the Blight-Ridden Viceroy effect ({0} Blightrot Cysts appear with every {1} raw or complex food produced). If you do, all your starting caravans will get {2} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Option2_De: Let it rest (<color=#FF8400>lose the Tarnished Necklace</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a Zitan Box</color>)
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Option2_To: Give away your Tarnished Necklace and you will receive a Zitan Box for the rest of this cycle: {0}
WorldEvent_BlightrotedViceroy_Reward: Though the creature's face is disfigured by grotesque, mutated growths, you can still see its eyes - and they shine with gratitude.
WorldEvent_BrassOrderEngineers_Desc: The narrow and winding path through the forest suddenly opens up, and a huge clearing appears before you. In the distance, you can see a group of Beavers hammering away at what appears to be a wooden scaffolding. Their uniforms bear the mark of the Brass Order.
WorldEvent_BrassOrderEngineers_Option2_D: Help them out (<color=#00D4FF>win before year {0} ends, with {1} Hearths upgraded to {2}</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {3}</color>)
WorldEvent_BrassOrderEngineers_Option2_T: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will get {1} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_BrassOrderEngineers_Reward: The engineers seem impressed with your skills. The oldest of them, a gloomy, mustached man, even shook your hand.
WorldEvent_CatastrophicExperiment_Desc: As you travel the wide and unusually even Royal Road, scattered alchemical tools catch your eye. The further you go, the more you find - until a familiar stench taints the air: Blightrot. Minutes later, you discover the source - a wrecked wagon, its frame crawling with Cysts. It seems you've stumbled upon the aftermath of an experiment gone awry.
WorldEvent_CatastrophicExperiment_Option: Complete the experiment (<color=#00D4FF>win after detonating a Blight Bomb</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain access to Fuel Rods</color>)

<color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> You gain access to <sprite name="[other] fuel rod"> Fuel Rods for the next {0} games. They are crafted in the Field Engineering Station and can be used to significantly boost the effectiveness of Rain Engines.
Send a scout (<color=#FF8400>lose {0} villager</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a Mining Automaton</color>)
WorldEvent_CatastrophicExperiment_Reward: You lived through the experiment - and can’t help but wonder what kind of mind imagined such a device.
WorldEvent_Chest_Generic_Desc: Ancient valuables or resources lost by another viceroy. Select the chest to collect its contents (it must be within your embarkation range).
WorldEvent_CloakedWanderer_Desc: "Always into the east" mumbles the wretched traveler, clutching something in his hand. Somehow you know that trying to take it by force would not be the wisest decision, but maybe he would be willing to part with it... for the right price.
WorldEvent_CloakedWanderer_Option1_Desc: Convince him (<color=#00D4FF>win with 3 Blood Flowers</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a Flame Altar blueprint for {0} games</color>)
WorldEvent_CloakedWanderer_Option1_Rewar: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> You receive a Flame Altar - an ancient building that grants access to temporary support abilities. Expires after {0} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_CloakedWanderer_Option1_Toolt: Start the game here with one Blood Flower clone in your settlement. Win while having at least 3 Blood Flower clones by the end, and you'll earn the Flame Altar blueprint - a powerful building that grants temporary blessings for your next {0} games.
WorldEvent_CloakedWanderer_Option2_Toolt: You will get {0} but your caravan will be haunted: {1}.
WorldEvent_CloakedWanderer_Reward: The Cloaked Wanderer stares at you in disbelief. Without a word, he silently offers you an obsidian tablet.
WorldEvent_CommendaContract_Desc: The guild has made you an offer. They've found an excellent spot for a trading hub and want you to establish it. In theory, only the Crown can command viceroys, but the guild has an unusual gift for finding clever ways around such antiquated laws.
WorldEvent_CommendaContract_Option1_Desc: Sign contract (<color=#00D4FF>win with trade routes</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0} and {1}</color>)
WorldEvent_CommendaContract_Option1_Tool: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will gain the following goods for the duration of this cycle: {1} and {2}.
WorldEvent_CommendaContract_Reward: The guild's representatives thank you for your help. But you can't shake the feeling that they initially promised you a higher salary...
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Desc: You encounter the wreckage of one of the Merchant Guild's famous airships. You can see a very busy crew running around it, trying to fix the ship and recover lost supplies. Suddenly, an old Beaver in a captain's blazer notices you, and yells out for help.
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option1_Condit: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> {0} To allow you to produce <sprite name="[we] fuel core"> Enriched Fuel, you will be given a new blueprint - the Field Engineering Station.
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option1_Desc: Provide fuel (<color=#00D4FF>deliver {0} and win before year {1} starts</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {2} and {3}</color>)
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option1_Toolti: {0} To allow you to produce <sprite name="[we] fuel core"> Enriched Fuel, you will be given a new blueprint - the Field Engineering Station. If you succeed, all your starting caravans will gain the following goods for the duration of this cycle: {1} and {2}.
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option2_Condit: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Complete a settlement that starts without any fuel (fuel from Embarkation Bonuses will also be removed).
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option2_Desc: Provide a substitute (<color=#00D4FF>win without starting fuel</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a blessing for {0} games</color>)
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option2_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> Traders arrive 25% faster, and perks and blueprints cost 25% less Amber. Expires after {0} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Option2_Toolti: Start the game here without any fuel (fuel from Embarkation Bonuses will also be removed). Upon winning, you will be given the Guild's Sigil perk (traders arrive 25% faster and their perks and blueprints cost 25% less) for the next {0} games.
WorldEvent_CrashedAirship_Reward: It seems that not too much time has passed - but to your surprise, the ship looks operational again.
WorldEvent_Cultists_Reward: You managed to convince the cultists to leave your caravan in peace. Let's just hope no one follows you...
WorldEvent_Eremite_Desc: Your caravan is suddenly stopped by an old Beaver in rugged clothing, blocking the passage. He seems to not have a care in the world, and won't move out of the way to let your wagons pass. His calm demeanor stands in stark contrast to the fast approaching storm clouds behind you. Perhaps you can learn from him?
WorldEvent_Eremite_Option1_Desc: Learn from him (<color=#FF8400>lose {0} years</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a blessing for {1} games</color>)
WorldEvent_Eremite_Option1_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> Blueprint rerolls cost 10 less <sprite name="[valuable] amber"> Amber. Expires after {0} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_Eremite_Option1_Tooltip: Lose {0} years off your current cycle. Gain the Eremite's Way perk (blueprint rerolls cost {1} less Amber) for the next {2} games.
WorldEvent_FireMoths_Desc: Villagers in this settlement have succumbed to the Disease of the Flame. Folks call such people Fire Moths, as those who lost themselves to the fire now sit around the hearth, staring at it aimlessly. You look into the flames for a while yourself, but there is nothing you can do for those wretched souls.
WorldEvent_FireMoths_Option1_Tooltip: All your starting caravans will gain {0} for the duration of this cycle, but some of your villagers ({1}) will be lost.
WorldEvent_FireMoths_Option2_Desc: Destroy the Hearth (<color=#FF8400>become cursed for 1 game</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0} and {1}</color>)
WorldEvent_FireMoths_Option2_Tooltip: All your starting caravans will gain {0} and {1} for the duration of this cycle, but the forest will rise against you: {2}
WorldEvent_FirstDawnCaravan_Desc: You come across a lively and bustling encampment of the First Dawn Company. One of the viceroys, sitting by the campfire, waves his hand in your direction, inviting you to join the group. Although it would be wiser not to trust the First Dawn, a moment's rest will surely do you good.
WorldEvent_FirstDawnCaravan_Option1_Tool: Lose {0}. All your starting caravans will have {1} more villagers for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_FirstDawnCaravan_Option2_Tool: Pay {0}, and all your starting caravans will gain {1} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Desc: As your villagers clear the ground for the new settlement, an old man emerges from the forest, waving his cane at you. A peculiar cat follows close behind. "Beware, fool!" the man cries. "Doom is coming soon! It will break your people's resolve and crush you! Prepare, or it will be the end of you!"
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Option1_Desc: Prepare for impending doom (<color=#00D4FF>win before year {0} ends, after fulfilling {1} service needs</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {2}</color>)
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Option1_Tooltip: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will gain {1} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Option2_Desc: Prove the forest is safe (<color=#00D4FF>rush {0} Dangerous/Forbidden Glades</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a purring ally for {1} games</color>)
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Option2_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> You receive a cat companion that boosts Global Resolve by 2 and increases the global double production chance by 5%. Expires after {0} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Option2_Tooltip: {0} If you do, a peculiar ally will join your caravan, adding +2 to Global Resolve and increasing your workers' chance of producing double yields by 5%. This effect will expire after {1} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Reward: "You have pushed back the doom that befell us, but I sense this is not the end", the old man says, lifting his cane with a trembling hand.
WorldEvent_FirstElder_Reward2: While the Elder mumbles something about insufferable fools, his cat slips onto your wagon and curls up comfortably on your seat.
WorldEvent_ForsakenGodsFollowers_Desc: As you make your way through the wilds, you hear a faint humming... An eerie song in a strange language. As you get closer, you see a circle of cloaked figures gathered around a strange obelisk. One of them points at you, and the others start slowly walking towards you.
WorldEvent_ForsakenGodsFollowers_Option1: Send "volunteers" (<color=#FF8400>lose {0} villagers</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {1} and {2} Reserve Embarkation Points</color>)
All your starting caravans will have {0} fewer villagers for the duration of this cycle, but you will gain {1}. You will also be rewarded with {2} Reserve Embarkation Points.
WorldEvent_ForsakenGodsFollowers_Option2: Join ritual (<color=#00D4FF>win before year {0} ends, with {1} dead villagers</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {2} and {3} Reserve Embarkation Points</color>)
{0} If you succeed, you will gain {2} Reserve Embarkation Points, and all your starting caravans will get {1} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_Gambler_Desc: You stumble upon a rugged man, wearing an old tattered cloak with the viceroys' insignia on it... and yet he has no caravan with him. He smiles at you, clearly relieved to see another living soul in this unforgiving wilderness. But he isn't asking you for food or clothing. Instead, he offers you a game of chance.
WorldEvent_Gambler_Option1_Condition: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Win a game with the Playing with Feelings effect (each season, a random species is favored).
WorldEvent_Gambler_Option1_Desc: Let fate decide (<color=#00D4FF>win with a random species favored each season</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0} and {1}</color>)
WorldEvent_Gambler_Option1_Tooltip: Win a game with the Playing with Feelings effect (each season, a random species is favored). If you succeed, all your starting caravans will gain the following goods for the duration of this cycle: {0} and {1}.
WorldEvent_Gambler_Option2_Condition: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Bet {0} and win with the Insane Gamble effect ({1} faster Impatience growth). If you don't succeed, the <sprite name=seal_fragments> Seal Fragments you bet will be lost.
WorldEvent_Gambler_Option2_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Resources.</color> You get your initial bet back ({0}) plus {1}.
WorldEvent_Gambler_Option2_Tooltip: Bet {0} and win with the Insane Gamble effect ({1} quicker Impatience growth). If you succeed, you'll get your initial bet back plus {2}. If you don't win, your bet ({0}) will be lost.
WorldEvent_Gambler_Reward: The gambler looks at you in disbelief. He seems furious, but at the same time insists that you make another bet with him.
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Desc: As you step out of the dense forest onto a vast, desolate plain, an eerie sight greets you - a ruined town shrouded in thick, clinging fog. In the distance, ghastly figures drift aimlessly along the horizon, as if searching for something. Suddenly, a few of them approach you. A distorted, echoing voice fills the air, recounting a grim tale of despair - a famine born of the Merchant Guild's insatiable greed.
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Option1_Desc: Punish the Guild (<color=#00D4FF>win before year {0} ends, after attacking 3 traders</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a blessing</color>)
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Option1_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> Calling traders to your settlement costs {0} less Impatience. Lasts for the entire cycle.
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Option1_Tooltip: {0} If you succeed, the cost of calling traders to your settlement will be reduced by {1} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Option2_Condition: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> {0} It will appear next to the Ancient Hearth and flee to the farthest Dangerous or Forbidden Glade possible (it will stay there much longer than stags normally do).
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Option2_Desc: Join the hunt (<color=#00D4FF>win after catching the Spectral Stag</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0}</color>)
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Option2_Tooltip: {0} It will appear next to the Ancient Hearth and flee to the farthest Dangerous or Forbidden Glade possible (it will stay there much longer than stags normally do). If you catch the stag and complete the settlement, all your starting caravans will get {1} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_GhostTown_Reward: The ghastly villagers fade away one by one. They say nothing, but there is a sense of relief in their wake.
WorldEvent_GhostTown2_Reward: It is too late to feed these poor souls, but the Spectral Stag hunt has brought them a measure of peace.
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Desc: People in these parts can take a lot, but whatever this poor bastard decided to do made the villagers snap. While some of them just sit in resignation, others are willing to push forward if you can prove to them that you actually care.
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Option1_Desc: Win them over (<color=#00D4FF>win with no-one leaving</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {1} villagers</color>)
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Option1_Tooltip: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will get {1} more villagers for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Option2_Conditi: <color=#FF8400>Curse.</color> Resolve drops {0} faster. Expires after {1} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Option2_Desc: Punish them (<color=#FF8400>become cursed for {0} games</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a cornerstone reroll</color>)
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Option2_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> All your settlements gain a cornerstone reroll. Lasts for the entire cycle.
WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Option2_Tooltip: For your loyalty, each of your settlements will receive an additional cornerstone reroll for the duration of this cycle. WorldEvent_HangedViceroy_Reward: You managed to convince some of the villagers to join your caravan.

WorldEvent_Loremaster_Desc: This Royal Loremaster was clearly sent here to locate something important to the Crown. After a few hours of trying, you are convinced there is no power in this world that would pry any clue about his goal from him. He has connections though, and is willing to pay for your help.
WorldEvent_Loremaster_Option1_Tooltip: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will gain the following goods for the duration of this cycle: {1} and {2}.

WorldEvent_MosquitoNest_Desc: Your scouts report a nearby nest of shelled mosquitos. You would rather step into the eye of the storm than come too close to their burrow, but shelled mosquitos form nests around old broken seals. Perhaps there is a way you can lure them away for a short while.
WorldEvent_MosquitoNest_Option1_Tooltip: Gain {0} in exchange for {1} (all your starting caravans will lose these goods for the duration of this cycle).
WorldEvent_MosquitoNest_Option2_Conditio: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Win a game with the Roaming Swarm effect (orders are unavailable, traders arrive {0} slower).
WorldEvent_MosquitoNest_Option2_Desc: Hunt the young ones (<color=#00D4FF>win with no orders and slower traders</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0} and {1} Reserve Embarkation Points</color>)
WorldEvent_MosquitoNest_Option2_Tooltip: Win a game with the Roaming Swarm effect (orders are unavailable, traders arrive {0} slower). If you succeed, you will earn {2} Reserve Embarkation Points, and all your starting caravans will get {1} for the duration of this cycle.

WorldEvent_RoamingFishmenTribe_Desc: You come across a bizarre sight - a group of 8 Fishmen wandering through the forest, led by an old soothsayer in a gray robe made of seaweed and shells. You feel inclined to run or take up a weapon, but the creatures don't seem hostile. One of them approaches you slowly, and in its black, fishy eyes, you can see a glimmer of curiosity mixed in with desperation.
WorldEvent_SadrathTheWise_Desc: You meet a hooded figure on the side of the road. Their face is shrouded in darkness, but you recognize some familiar features. As the creature approaches you, the name of Sothur immediately jumps to mind... yet this isn't him. Another ancient one, perhaps? The man smiles gently, revealing a row of disturbingly sharp teeth.
WorldEvent_SadrathTheWise_Option1_Desc: Ask for his help (<color=#FF8400>pay {0}</color>, <color=#00FF15>a chosen World Map modifier will appear</color>)

WorldEvent_SadrathTheWise_Option1_Toolti: Pay {0}, and a World Map modifier of your choice will appear in place of this World Event.
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Desc: Your caravan stumbles upon a long and somber procession, carrying a body encased in a block of amber. Another viceroy perished, attempting the trial to join the Queen's Hands. The mourners ask you not to disturb the forest, and ensure their safe passage back to the Citadel.
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Option1_Desc: Pay respects (<color=#00D4FF>open {0} or fewer Dangerous/Forbidden Glades</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {1} and {2}</color>)
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Option1_Tool: {0} If you succeed, all your starting caravans will gain the following goods for the duration of this cycle: {1} and {2}.
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Option2_Desc: Join the funeral (<color=#00D4FF>win after completing the Funeral Feast event</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a Feast Hall blueprint for {0} games</color>)
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Option2_Rewa: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> You receive a Feast Hall blueprint. {0}
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Option2_Tool: Start the game with a Feast Hall blueprint. Build it, complete all three stages of the Funeral Feast, and win the game. If you succeed, you will receive the Feast Hall blueprint for the next {0} games (a service building where villagers can fulfill their need for Brawling and Treatment).
WorldEvent_SomberProcession_Reward: The mourners thank you for your sympathy.
WorldEvent_SormbirdEgg_Desc: Cutting through the thicket, your caravan stumbles upon a stormbird egg. Your instincts scream to leave it in peace and flee before its mother comes back, but... who hasn't dreamed of having a pet stormbird, at least for a while?
WorldEvent_StormAntsColumn_Desc: An enormous column of Storm Ants stretches in both directions. Large as a Beaver's fist, they've made entire armies wait for days. On a large tree nearby, right in the middle of the ant column, you can see a trader with his guard, screaming for help. But only one thing in the world would make the Storm Ants change course. Food.
WorldEvent_StormAntsColumn_Option1_Condi: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Complete a settlement that starts without any food (food from Embarkation Bonuses will also be removed).
WorldEvent_StormAntsColumn_Option1_Desc: Dump your food (<color=#00D4FF>win without starting food</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {0}</color>)
WorldEvent_StormAntsColumn_Option1_Toolt: Start the game here without any food (food from Embarkation Bonuses will also be removed). Upon winning, all your starting caravans will get {0} for the duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_StormAntsColumn_Reward: The distraction worked. The merchant and his guard managed to escape.
WorldEvent_StormbirdEgg_Option1_Conditio: <color=#FF8400>Curse.</color> An angry Stormbird mother will follow your caravan ({0} to Global Resolve during the Storm). Expires after {1} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEvent_StormbirdEgg_Option1_Desc: Steal the egg (<color=#FF8400>become cursed for {0} games</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain {1}</color>)
WorldEvent_StormbirdEgg_Option1_Tooltip: All your starting caravans will gain {0} for the duration of this cycle, but an angry Stormbird mother will follow your caravan (-2 to Global Resolve during the Storm) until you successfully complete {1} settlements.
WorldEvent_StormbirdEgg_Option2_Reward: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> Global production speed is increased by {0}. Lasts for the entire cycle.
WorldEvent_StormbirdEgg_Option2_Tooltip: Lose {0}. In return, you'll get a {1} bonus to global production speed for the entire duration of this cycle.
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Desc: As you push through the dense foliage, you notice movement in the distance - massive trees swaying, then crashing to the ground. With a few scouts at your side, you creep closer. And after a short, tense walk, the source of the chaos emerges from the mist - a Tree Grazer.
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option1_Condition: <color=#00D4FF>Objective.</color> Win a game with a Tree Grazer in your settlement - a giant beast that consumes one tree every 20 seconds, opening up to a maximum of 10 glades.
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option1_Desc: Follow the beast (<color=#00D4FF>win with a Tree Grazer in your settlement</color>, <color=#00FF15>gain a Rainpunk Shredder</color>)
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option1_Reward: You faced the Tree Grazer - and lived to tell the tale.
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option2_Desc: Investigate the aftermath (<color=#00D4FF>win with 2 Dangerous Glades already open</color>, <color=#00FF15>unlock Woodcutters' Camp upgrades for {0} games</color>)
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option2_Reward: You not only survived but gained rare insight from observing this magnificent beast.
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option2_Tooltip: Start the game here with 2 Dangerous Glades already open (plus 2 to 3 Small Glades). If you succeed, you'll unlock the option to upgrade Woodcutters' Camps for the next {0} games.
WorldEvent_TreeGrazer_Option2_TreeGrazer: <color=#00FF15>Cycle effect.</color> You unlock the ability to upgrade Woodcutters' Camps. Expires after {0} successful settlements in the current cycle.
WorldEventRewardsPopup_RewardsDesc: You receive a reward for successfully solving the event.
WorldUI_CapitalPanel_GoalsButton_LockedT: Unlock Obsidian Archive Level 1 to access deeds.
WorldUI_CapitalPanel_SealPanel_Tooltip: Reforging this seal increased the duration of the cycle by {0} years.
WorldUI_CapitalPanel_SealPanel_Tooltip_N: Reforging a specific seal for the first time will reduce the influence of the Sealed Ones on the surface world, and permanently increase the time between Blightstorms.
WorldUI_CapitalUpgradesPopup_Preview_Buy: You must buy all previous upgrades from this branch and reach the required level.
WorldUI_CapitalUpgradesPopup_Preview_Emp: Select an upgrade to display the preview.
WorldUI_CustomGame_Desc: To challenge yourself and improve your skills, you can embark on a Training Expedition. You can choose any set of starting conditions, but Training Expeditions yield no rewards, don't count towards Deeds, and won't progress the Blightstorm Cycle.
WorldUI_CustomGames_ButtonLocked: Upgrade the Obsidian Archive in the Smoldering City to access Training Expeditions.
WorldUI_CustomGames_Modifiers_Tooltip_De: Not all modifiers will work in all conditions, and some might automatically be discarded when starting a game. For example, Wine Shortage when there are no Beavers, or Dangerous Lands combined with Forbidden Lands.
WorldUI_CustomGames_SeasonalEffects_Tool: The regular storm effect (Looming Darkness) is active in every game.
WorldUI_CustomGames_TradeTowns_Tooltip_D: You can only select towns that are currently on your World Map. When saving a template, towns are saved based on their position on the World Map.
WorldUI_CycleEnd_ClosedSeal_Tooltip_Desc: According to custom, successfully closing a seal grants you royal tax relief. You gain an additional {0} of all Citadel Resources obtained during this cycle.
WorldUI_CycleEnd_Description: The Blightstorm is coming. Your settlements have been abandoned, and people are returning to the Citadel. In this moment of reckoning, the Queen will reward her most faithful and resourceful subjects.
WorldUI_CycleEnd_Description_Short: The Blightstorm is coming. Your settlements have been abandoned, and people are returning to the Citadel.
WorldUI_CycleOverHeader: The Blightstorm is almost here, so no further expeditions can embark during this cycle. Select the compass icon to finish the cycle.
WorldUI_CycleOverHeader_Ironman: Your trial is complete. Head to the Smoldering City and enter the Citadel to join the ranks of the Queen's Hands.
WorldUI_CycleOverHeader_PreSeal: The Blightstorm is coming. If your last settlement is within range of an Ancient Seal, you can embark one last time and try to reforge it. If not, press the compass button and wait out the storm in the Smoldering City.
WorldUI_CycleOverHeader_PreSeal_Demo: The Blightstorm is coming. Reforging seals is not possible in the demo, so the only thing you can do is press the compass button to restart the cycle.
WorldUI_CycleOverHeader_SkipToSealTip: You have enough <sprite name="seal_fragments"> Seal Fragments and are within range of an Ancient Seal, so you can reforge it. If you wish, you can skip the rest of the cycle by pressing the compass button in the bottom right corner of the screen.
WorldUI_DailyChallange_ButtonLocked: Upgrade the Obsidian Archive in the Smoldering City to access Daily Expeditions.
WorldUI_DailyChallenge_Desc: Once per day, you can join the Royal Expedition and venture into the strangest of lands, where the Ancient Seals are broken and reality has been distorted.
WorldUI_DailyChallenge_NoDeedsInfo: Deeds are disabled in Daily Expeditions
WorldUI_DifficultyTooltip_Hard: Recommended for players who already know the rules of the game well and like a medium challenge.
WorldUI_DifficultyTooltip_Impossible: Recommended for very advanced players who want to face additional challenges and deal with difficult tasks. Gateway to Prestige difficulties.
WorldUI_DifficultyTooltip_Normal: Recommended for beginner players who want to slowly learn the mechanics of the game. A good starting point after the Tutorial.
WorldUI_DifficultyTooltip_Prestige: A series of progressing difficulty levels. Winning a Prestige run unlocks further Prestige levels. Each level adds a new challenge modifier. Recommended for players who have mastered the game.
WorldUI_DifficultyTooltip_VeryHard: Recommended for advanced players who want to face additional challenges.
WorldUI_EmbarkScreen_EarlyEndMarker_Tool: You are embarking on an expedition to the Sealed Forest early. Your mere presence there will trigger the end of the cycle, regardless of how many years are left. You have only one chance to reforge the seal before the Blightstorm comes.
WorldUI_FieldPanel_ModifierRewards_Toolt: Allows you to choose one of three prizes: 5 Seal Fragments, 2 fields of additional Embarkation Range, or 4 Reserve Embarkation Points.

WorldUI_FieldTooltip_SealDesc: This area contains a weakening ancient seal. At the end of the cycle, if the seal is within your embarkation range, you can try to reforge it.
WorldUI_FieldTooltip_TooSoonForSealed: You can venture here only once, at the very end of the cycle.

You're about to meet Aunt Lori. What's your relation to her?
 
 (This setting can always be changed in the options menu.)
WorldUI_GoalsPopup_Slot_OnlyInCitadel: Deed rewards can't be collected in settlement mode.
WorldUI_HomePopupButton_LockedTooltip: You'll get your own place in the Smoldering City by completing the deed: {0}. Remember to claim your reward after completing the deed.
WorldUI_IronmanContractPopup_Desc:
This sacred contract, willingly entered into by the Viceroy, marks the beginning of the Queen's Hand Trial - a crucible of unparalleled challenge and consequence. 

The loss of a settlement or the inability to reforge the Adamantine Seal within one Blightstorm Cycle will not be met with mercy but with swift and irrevocable execution.

This undertaking is reserved only for the elite - those of indomitable spirit and unwavering resolve, where there is no room for complaint or lamentation.

Should the Viceroy emerge victorious from the Queen's Hand Trial, they will be awarded the coveted title of Queen's Hand. This reward goes beyond mere honors - the triumphant Viceroy is also granted a rare audience with the Queen herself. 

May the Holy Flame guide you, and the unrelenting rain bear witness to this solemn covenant.
WorldUI_IronmanResult_Desc_Lost_FailedRu: News of your failure reached the Citadel much faster than your caravan...
WorldUI_IronmanResult_Desc_Lost_Sufix: Your execution is quick and unceremonious. The last thing you feel is the warm rain on your neck, before everything goes dark.
WorldUI_IronmanResult_Desc_Lost_Years: The Blightstorm is coming, and with it, your downfall.
WorldUI_IronmanResult_Desc_Won: You have succeeded. You've prevailed where so many have failed. Was it worth it?
WorldUI_MetaCalendar_EarlyFinishDecision: This will skip the rest of the cycle, allowing you to play one last game near an available seal. This action cannot be undone.

WorldUI_MetaCalendar_FinishButton_SkipTo: Wait until the end of the cycle.
WorldUI_MetaCalendar_FinishButton_ToEarl: It's too early to finish the cycle. Viceroys are obliged to establish settlements until the Blightstorm is almost upon them.
WorldUI_MetaCalendar_IronmanForfeitToolt: By finishing this cycle early, you are condemning yourself to death. There is no going back.

WorldUI_ModifierPickPopup_BlockedByOther: This modifier is blocked by another modifier on one of the adjacent fields.
WorldUI_ModifierRewardsPopup_Desc: "I salute you for your achievements, Viceroy! Many who have entered these lands never came back. As is tradition, you can petition the Crown for a resupply."
WorldUI_ModifierRewardsPopup_Footer: This choice has to be made before starting a new expedition.
WorldUI_SealContracts_SlotTooltip_Defaul: This Seal ({0}) can be found {1} fields from the Citadel. It requires {2} and must be attempted on {3} difficulty or higher.

WorldUI_SealFragments_Description: Legend says that the seals can never be broken, but these shards tell a different story. Fragments are needed to venture into the Sealed Forest at the end of every cycle to reforge the ancient seal. Any leftovers must be sold back to the Crown.

WorldUI_WorldTutorialsHUD_Desc: Here you can replay tutorial missions and unlock additional scenarios that will explain the more complex aspects of the game. Tutorial towns have no effect on the Blightstorm Cycle and don't appear on the World Map, but will grant you some resources for completion.

News_Update1_10_Content: This update introduces three new World Map modifiers (including one where you play with four species), an overhaul of the hauler system (pun intended), new deeds, and a wide range of UI improvements inspired by community feedback.

ModifierEffect_4Races_Desc: A revered site commemorating the peace forged after the Great Civil War. Your settlement can have four species at once, but you cannot choose newcomer groups. Each Drizzle season, you gain {0} random villager for each discovered glade (including the starting glade).
ModifierEffect_RandomSeasonDuration_Desc: An ominous structure made from a material not known to contemporary scholars. Clouds swirl around the tip of this giant tower. Seasons have random durations.
ModifierEffect_OneInitialVillagerPerRace: By royal decree, this land belongs to the Merchant Guild, and only its appointed representatives may settle here. You begin with a single villager per species. Additional villagers from Embarkation Bonuses are not granted.
Deed_WinWithAllNeeds_4Races_Desc: Ensure all villagers have all their needs fulfilled simultaneously while having four species in one settlement. Needs met in the Commons don’t count.
WorldUI_CustomGames_Races_Tooltip_Desc: Settlements have three species by default. In Training Expeditions, you can choose up to four. Unselected species are filled randomly (up to three total). To play with four, you must select them manually.
